26. It appears that sub-section (4) of section 3 the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000 is similar to sub-section (3) of section 4 of the Admiralty Jurisdiction of the High Court’s Ordinance 1980, in Pakistan which reads as follows:

"(3) In any case in which there is a maritime lien or other charge on any ship, aircraft or other property the Admiralty Jurisdiction of the High Court may be invoked by an action in rem against that ship, aircraft or property."

"(4) In the case of any such claim as mentioned in clause (e) to (h) and (j) to (q) of sub-section (2) of section 3, being a claim arising in connection with a ship, where the person who would be liable on, the claim in an action in personam was when the cause of action arose, the owner or charterer of, or in possession or in control of the ship, the Admiralty jurisdiction of the High Court may, whether the claim gives rise to maritime lien on the ship or not, be invoked by an action in rem against-

(a) that ship, if at the time when the action is brought it is beneficially owned as respects to majority shares therein by that person; or

(b) any other ship which, at the time when the action is brought, is beneficially owned as aforesaid."

27. In the present case I have already observed that the ship is still lying afloat and which is at the time of filing of the suit and order of arrest lying in the Jahanabad, Kadamrasul, Sitakunda, Chittagong. It may be noted that under sub-section (3) it has been expressly provided that in any case in which there is a maritime lien, the Admiralty Jurisdiction High Court may be invoked by an action in rem against the ship, Aircraft or other property,

28. It may also be pointed out that the above sub-section (4) of section 4 of the Ordinance clearly excludes the case of maritime lien by referring to whether claim gives rise to a maritime lien on the ship or not. In other words, the right to sue in rem by virtue of sub-section (4) of section 4 of the Ordinance, is in addition to the right of maritime lien and same is independent of the above provision. In this connection reliance is placed in the case of Global Shipping Co. (Pvt) Limited vs MV Sea Elite, reported in 1985 CLC 1569. In the above case, it has been held that action in rem to maintain a maritime hen is independent of the above provision of sub-section (4) of section 4 of the Ordinance.

29. In this connection it is necessary to refer paragraphs 65 and 85 of the well known book British Shipping Laws, 1980 Edition, Volume 14 by Dr Thomas which reads as follows:—

"85. Section 3(4) and maritime liens—In section 3(4) it is expressly provided that the sub-section is applicable whether the claim gives rise to maritime lien or not. Notwithstanding this reference section 3(3) continues to be the principal jurisdictional provision with regard to maritime liens. The significance of the reference to maritime liens in section 3(4) is to make it clear that an alternative action in rem against a sister ship is equally applicable to claims in the nature of maritime liens, Where an incumbranced ship is, therefore, not readily available a maritime lien may alternatively proceed in rem against another ship in the same beneficial ownership. Section 3(4) does not work any change in the nature of a maritime lien nor does it extend the concept of a maritime lien. The alternative right in rem is the nature of a statutory right of action in rem and the availability of the right is dependent on the provisions of section 3(4) being satisfied."

"65. The adoption of the proceduraliest thesis has resulted in the action in rem acquiring a significant quasi-personal flavor. It has also had a profound influence on the development of law. Nonetheless the thesis has its limitations and would appear to be inapplicable to rights in rem which accrue under maritime liens which arise independently of personal liability on the part of a res owner."

30. Reference may also be made to relevant observations from paragraph 14 of the above book, which reads as under:

"The question of the personal liability of a res owner assumes significance only in relation to the accrual of a maritime lien. It has no further application and, in particular, does not operate to restrict the right of a maritime lienee to arrest a res in the hands of a purchaser, In bitch a case there clearly exists no personal liability on the part of the subsequent purchaser but this fact does not dissolve the right of a maritime lienee."

31. I am, therefore, inclined to hold that sub-section (4) of section 4 of the Ain is not applicable to the instant case and the above suit are competent even against the defendant No. 9, the purchaser of the vessel as the maritime lien was attached to the vessel and the vessel is now in afloat condition and lying in the Jahanarabad Yard, Sitakunda when the above suit was filed and order of arrest was passed.

32. It appears that the plaintiff filed the present suit invoking the Admiralty Jurisdiction of this court under section 4(3) of the Ain in an action in rem to enforce maritime lien. A suit in rem does not change its nature and character because the owners and parties interested in have been identified and impleaded in the plaint. In the present suit the ship (res) has been impleaded as defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 2 has been described as "owners and parties interested in" the vessel of defendant No. 1 and the defendant No. 9 as current owner was impleaded in the suit. The fact that the current owners of the ship, defendant No. 9 have been impleaded and identified in the suit does not mean that suit ceases to be action in rem.

33. In the case reported in PLD 1986 Quetta 54 which was clearly an action in rem and similar to the present case, the defendant No. 1 was the vessel (res) the defendant No. 2 was the previous owners of the vessel and defendant No. 4 was the purchasers of the vessel. Held was held in that case that the court has jurisdiction in the action in rem and the said suit were decreed. Similarly in an unreported case this Admiralty Court decreed the Admiralty Suit No. 24 of 2005 in an action in rem by the judgment and decree dated 14-8-2012 where the defendant No. 1 vessel MV Al-Giorgis ex MV Arva Mary was the vessel (res), and defendant Nos. 5, 6 and 6B were previous owners and the defendant No. 6A was the purchaser or present owner.

34. It further appears that the plaintiff does not invoke the jurisdiction of this court in personam under section 5 of the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000. Therefore, there is no need to establish that the cause of action arose in the internal or territorial waters of Bangladesh. The action is not action in personam and which is clear from the plaint that the plaintiff have not sought an arrest or attachment of the property of the defendants owners but only sought an arrest of the ship (res) -defendant No. 1 in a suit arising from an action in rem to enforce a maritime lien on the arrested vessel, MV Athens (ex MV Hansa).

35. It cannot be denied that the Admiralty Court in Bangladesh prior to the enforcement of the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000 (Act XLIII of 2000) were exercising admiralty jurisdiction in order to enforce the maritime lien and, therefore, by virtue of the above proviso, the above jurisdiction remained intact apart from the express jurisdiction conferred on the High Court under the Ain by sub-section (3) of section 4 which provides that admiralty jurisdiction can be exercised in any case, in which, there is a maritime lien. Thus the plaintiff's claim arising from maritime lien against the defendant vessel prima-facie fall under section 4(3) of the said Ain.

<u>36. After meticulous examination of the above sections it transpires that subject to the limitation placed by section 5 of the Ain, the Admiralty Jurisdiction of the High Court may in all cases be invoked by an action in personam. Section 4 of the Ain provides the mode of exercise of Admiralty Jurisdiction. In the cases mentioned in clauses (Ka) to (Ga) and (Da) of sub-section (2) of section 3 be invoked by an action in rem against the ship or property in question under section 4(2) of the Ain. In any case in which there is a maritime lien or other charge on any ship, aircraft or other property of the amount claimed, the Admiralty Jurisdiction of the High Court may be invoked under section 4(3) of the Ain. Yet in another class of cases mentioned in clauses (Gha) to (Tha) of sub-section (2) of section 3 can be invoked by an action in rem against the ship provided the person who would be liable for such claim in an action in personam was, when the cause of action arose, the owner or charterer of or in possession or control of the ship and at the time when the action is brought that person beneficially owns in respect all shares in the ship or any other ship which, at the time when the action is brought, is beneficially owned as aforesaid. It may also be pointed out that sub-section (4) of section 4 of the Ain clearly excludes the case of maritime lien by referring to whether claim gives rise to a maritime lien on the ship or not. In other words, the right to sue in rem by virtue of sub-section (4) of section 4 of the Ain, is in addition to the right of maritime lien.</u>

37. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, relevant provisions of the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000, and considering the decisions cited above, I do not find any merit in this application.

38. In the result, the application for vacating the order of arrest is rejected without any order as to cost.

The suit is now fixed on 17-3-2014 for appearance of the defendant Nos. 1-8.

End.

lawyer:
Ahsanul Karim with Aminul Hoque, Advocates ------ For the Petitioner.
Md Mokleshur Rahman, DAG ------ For the Respondents.
parties:
Shafiul Azam (Md) ------ Petitioner
Vs
The Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Naima Haider J: In this application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh a Rule was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the respondents shall not be directed to release the awarded compensation in favour of the petitioner on account of acquisition of the scheduled land and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The facts necessary for disposal of the Rule, in brief are:

One Syed Hasan Ali was the absolute owner of the said land which devolved on his only son, Syed Mohammad Ali after his demise. Thereafter, the said Syed Mohammad Ali died leaving his only son, Syed Ahsan Ali and his wife Syeda Hosne Ara Begum as his heirs who sold the said land to Md Akkas Ali (father of the petitioner) and Md Abdus Sobhan vide registered Sale Deed No. 2926 dated 7-2-1973. Some clerical mistake having been crept up in the sale deed and Syed Ahsan Ali and Syeda Hosne Ara Begum executed an amended deed vide Registered Amended Deed No. 30146 dated 10-12-1976 before the office of Sadar Sub-Register Dhaka. Md Akkas Ali and Md Abdus Sobhan after having become the absolute owner of the said land applied to mutate their names in the record of rights maintained by the Government. At that stage the said Md Akkas Ali and Md. Abdus Sobhan came to know that in SA Record the scheduled land was recorded in Khas Khatian No. 1 as a road whereas the scheduled land was pond and not a road. In such situation they filed Mutation Case No. 1428 (shoi) of 1977-78 before the Circle Officer, Dhaka who vide Order dated 1-9-1977 directed Tahshildar to give detail report to that effect. The Tahshildar in his report stated that the title of the land vested in Md Akkas Ali and Md Abdus Sobhan and the said land was never a Khas land of the Government. The Tahshildar clearly stated that the land was wrongly recorded in the Akkas Ali and Md Abdus Sobhan in connection with the said land.

3. The Circle Officer also sought opinion from Government pleader who also opined that the said land could be mutated in the names of Md Akkas Ali and Md Abdus Sobhan. Thereafter the Circle Officer, Dhaka vide Order dated 19-10-1977 allowed of the Mutation Case No. 1428 (Shoi) of 1977-78 in favour of the said Md Akkas Ali and Md Abdus Sobhan and mutated the names of Md Akkas Ali and Md Abdus Sobhan in respect of the said land and directed Tahshildar to make necessary correction in the record of right and realise the fees for mutation of their names as per law. The said Md Akkas Ali and Md Abdus Sobhan paid the fees for mutation and up-to-date rents on 25-10-1977. The Government never preferred any appeal against the said order dated 19-10-1977 passing the said Mutation Case. Thereafter, their names were also recorded in the R.S. Khatian. In the year 1999 and 2011 their names were recorded in the field survey record and Dhaka City Survey record respectively. Md Akkas Ali died on 26-3-2004 leaving behind his son the petitioner, his wife and his five daughters as his heirs. While the petitioner was in peaceful possession of the said land the Government initiated LA Proceeding No. 13/2010-2011 for acquisation of the said land. The petitioner and other heirs of Md Akkas Ali filed application for getting compensation in respect of the said land. Upon receipt of the said application, the Assistant Land Officer, Gulshan Land Office, Dhaka vide Memo dated 11-4-2012 informed the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Gulshan Circle, Dhaka that the Government does not have any interest in the land. The said Memo dated 11-4-2012 was also endorsed by Assistant Officer (Land), Gulshan land Office, Dhaka. However, as per the direction of the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Gulshan Circle, Dhaka, the Kanungo and Surveyor submitted a report on the same day i.e. on 12-4-2012 on the said land stating that 1.23 acres of land in SA Dag No. 2465 involved in Mutation Case No. 4363/11 has earlier been recorded in No. 1 Khas Khatian and therefore, Government has interest in this land. After receiving the report of the Kanungo and Surveyor, the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Gulshan Circle, in total disregard of the Memo dated 11-4-2012 of the Assistant Land Officer, Gulshan Land Office, vide Memo No. সঃকঃভুঃ(গুল)-১৫ dated 15-4-2012 forwarded the report of the Kanungo and Surveyor.

4. Thereafter, the Land Acquisition Officer, Dhaka vide Memo No. 05.41.2600.033.14.001.11-452 dated 24-5-2012 requested the Government Pleader (GP), Dhaka to give his opinion as to whether compensation can be given to those persons whose names were mutated in respect of the land in RS Dag Nos. 6132, 6133 and 6134 (subsequently City Survey Dag Nos. 9662, 9663, 9665 and 17355) which was earlier recorded in the No. 1 Khas Khatian as SA Dag No. 3465. The Government Pleader (GP), Dhaka after considering all the documents and record gave detailed opinion on the scheduled land on 5-6-2012. The Government Pleader (GP) in his report dated 5-6-2012 in clear terms stated that SA Record was duly amended and the names of the predecessor of the petitioner was duly mutated in relation to the scheduled land. In the said opinion, it is also stated that the names of the petitioner and other heirs of the said Md Akkas Ali having been published in the official gazette after the last City Survey, they are entitled to get the compensation in relation to the said land.

5. In the aforesaid circumstances, having no other way, the petitioner sent a Notice Demanding Justice on 22-7-2012 requesting the respondent Nos. 1, 2 and 3 to release 'the awarded compensation in respect of the scheduled land in favour of the heirs of the said Md Akkas Ali. But the respondent Nos. 1, 2 and 3 did not take any action in this regard.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the inaction of respondent Nos. 1, 2 and 3 the petitioner has moved this Court and obtained the instant Rule Nisi.

7. The respondents did not enter appearance by filing affidavit-in-opposition controverting the statements made in the writ petition.

8. Mr Md Mokleshur Rahman learned Deputy Attorney-General, however, made oral submissions in this Rule.

9. Mr Ahsanul Karim, Advocate appeared with Mr Khairul Alam Choudhury and Ms Farzana Khan on behalf of the petitioner submitted that the Circle Officer vides Order dated 19-10-1997 ordered that the said land can be mutated in the name of Md Akkas Ali and Md Abdus Sobhan. Mr Ahsanul Karim then took us to Dhaka City Survey Record (Annexure D1) published in the names of Md Akkas Ali and another in connection with the said land under section 144(7) of the State Acquisition Tenancy Act, 1950 (the said Act). He submitted that under section 144(7) of the said Act the Revenue Officer finally framed the record and caused the record finally published in the prescribed manner and the publication of such record has the conclusive evidence that the record has been duly prepared. Therefore, the record having been published in the names of Md Akkas Ali and another, such record provides us with the conclusive evidence of the aforementioned. He further submitted that under section 144A of the said Act, The Dhaka City Survey Record (Annexure D1) has the presumption of its correctness. The said land was also mutated in the name of the petitioner and other heirs of Md Akkas Ali and Md Abdus Sobhan (Annexure E) wherein the Assistant Commissioner (Land) gave a declaration that the land in question is not a khas land. Mr Karim then submitted that the Deputy Commissioner Dhaka served a notice upon the petitioner and others under section 7 of the Acquisition and Requisition of the Immovable Property Ordinance, 1882 (the said Ordinance) for compensation. Mr Ahsanul Karim referred to the report of Land Office (Annexure H) dated 12-4-2012 which evidenced that the land was never a khas land. Mr Ahsanul Karim lastly submitted that the Gazzette Notification published by the Government dated 12-4-2009 which also evidenced that the land in question is not a khas land and the respondents were under obligation to pay the compensation as notified day them in their notice under section 7 of the said Ordinance.

10. Mr Md Mokleshur Rahman, learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the respondents contested the Rule without however filing any affidavit-in-opposition He submitted that the petitioner is not entitled to get any compensation out of the LA Proceeding but found it difficult to oppose the Rule.

11. We have considered the writ petition and Annexures contained therein, the supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioner and the submissions made by the advocates of both the parties. We considered the Annexure "B" of the writ petition, from which it appears vide order dated 19-10-1977 allowed the Mutation Case No. 1428 (Shoi) of 1977-78 in favour of the predecessors of the petitioner and that the Circle Office approved the land was mutated in the names of Md Akkas Ali and another after correction of the record. From Annexure 'C' it appears that the land was mutated in the name of the said persons. From Annexure 'C1' it appears that the Government received rent from the said Md. Akkas Ali and another. From Annexure 'D' it appears that the said land was mutated in the names of Md Akkas Ali and another. From Annexure 'D1' it appears that Dhaka City Survey Report was published in the names of Md Akkas Ali and another in connection with the said land in question under section 144(7) of the said Act. The land Assistant Officer, Gulshan land office by Memo dated 12-4-2012 (Annexure H) sent report to the office of Assistant Commissioner (Land) Gulshan Circle, Dhaka stating that Government has no interest in the said land. The Office of Assistant Commissioner (Annexure I to the writ petition) vide report dated 12-4-2012 stated that from the report of Land Officer it appears that 1.23 acres of land in Dag No. 2465, Mouza-Vatara is khas land. It is a settled principle of law as communicated by the Hon'ble Appellate Division in the case of The Chairman, Board of Investment vs Bay Trawling Limited, 3 MLR (AD) 54 = 51 DLR (AD) 79 that any decision of one lawful Governmental authority is  binding upon all other Governmental authorities.

<u>12. Hence, we are of the view that Circle Officer being a Governmental Authority passed the order dated 19-10-1977 mutating the said land in favour of the predecessors of petitioner divesting any right, title or interest of Government in the said land, against which the Government never preferred any appeal and/ or took any step before any forum for setting aside the said order and, as such the said decision dated 19-10-1977 of Circle Officer is binding upon all other Governmental Authorities and the Government itself. So the said report is absolutely malafide and colourable exercise of power because the Land Officer (Annexure H) stated that the said land is not a khas land. The Land Acquisition Officer to resolve the issue vide Memo dated 24-5-2012 sought opinion from the Government pleader (Annexure J to the writ petition) and the Government pleader by his opinion dated 5-6-2012 clearly opined that the Government has no interest in the land in question. Hence, we are of the view that the respondent without due process of law has not paid the awarded compensation to the petitioner in connection with the said land.</u>

13. Considering all the facts and circumstances made hereinbefore, we find merit in the Rule. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute. The respondents are directed to pay the awarded compensation to the petitioner in connection with the said land (46.94 decimals of land in Mouza-Vatara, SA Plot No. 2465, Mutation Khatian No. 11077, RS Khatian No. 17, corresponding to Plot Nos. 6132, 6133 and 6134) within two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment and order.

There is no order as to costs.

End.

lawyer:
Md. Khurshid Alam Khan with Tushar Kanti Roy, Advocates ------ For the Petitioner 
Md Mutahar Hossain with Ali Asif Khan, Md Muddasir Hossain and Majedul Quader, Advocates ------ For the Respondent No. 3
parties:
Serajul Haque (Md) ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Election Appellate Tribunal, Narsigndi and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Naima Haider J: In this application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, Rule was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 8-1-2013 passed by Election Appellate Tribunal and District Judge, Narsingdi, Respondent No. 1 in Election Revision No. 23 of 2012 affirming the judgment and order dated 17-9-2012 passed by Election Tribunal and Senior Assistant Judge, Sadat Court, Narsingdi, Respondent No. 2 directed to open the gunny bag and recount the ballot papers before the court in presence of the lawyers of both the parties as contained in Annexures-E and E-1 should not be passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The facts necessary for the disposal of the Rule, in brief, are as follows:

The petitioner is the incumbent Chairman of the Bashgari Union Parishad, police station- Raipura, District-Narsigndi having been elected in the Union Parishad Election on 18-6-2011. The said Bashgari Union is demarcated into 9 (Nine) Wards and each wards has its own Polling Centre. The election of the Bashgari Union Parishad was held on 18-6-2011 and all votes were soiled and counted by the officers of the Election Commission. There were 9(Nine) polling centres, 1(One) for each ward, within the Bashgari Union Parishad including the disputed Bashgari New Model High School for Ward No. 3. The respondent No. 4 was appointed by respondent No. 6 vide Memo dated 11-6-2011 (Annexure-"X" to the Application for vacating the order of stay filed by respondent No. 3) as Presiding Officer of the aforesaid disputed polling centre, namely, Bashgari New Model High School under Ward No. 3 of the Bashgari Union.

3. The petitioner along with respondent Nos. 3, 11 and 12 contested for the post of Chairman of the said Union Parishad. Prior to the election, on 12-6-2011 the respondent No. 3 raised objection before the concerned authorities, including the respondent Nos. 6 and 7, to change the Presiding Officers of 3 (Three) Polling Centres, including the respondent No. 4 at the aforesaid disputed polling centre, since the respondent No. 4's honesty and sincerity vis-a-vis his professional responsibility/commitment were questioned by all and, hence, the respondent No. 4's neutrality was disputed by all.

4. On 18-6-2011, upon completion of the aforesaid election, respondent No. 4 prepared the prescribed statement showing the result of the vote count for the aforesaid disputed polling centre and supplied it to respondent No. 6. The petitioner was later declared as Chairman of the Bashgari Union Parishad having defeated respondent No. 3 by a margin of 23 (Twenty-Three) votes; the petitioner obtained 2951 (Two Thousand Nine Hundred and Fifty-One) votes, whereas the respondent No. 3 obtained 2928 (Two Thousand Nine Hundred and Twenty-Eight) votes. As a result, the Election Commission published a Gazette on 3-8-2011 declaring the petitioner as the Chairman of the Bashgari Union Parishad, District-Narsingdi.

5. On 23-8-2011 being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the result of the aforesaid disputed polling centre, the respondent No. 3 filed the Election Tribunal Case No. 24 of 2011 ("the said Election Tribunal Case") before the learned Election Tribunal and Senior Assistant Judge, Narsingdi ("the learned Election Tribunal below") praying for: (i) cancellation of the purported result of election of Bashgari Union Parishad held on 18-6-2011 and (ii) declaration that the respondent No. 3 is the newly elected Chairman of the said Union Parishad.

6. On 31-10-2011, the petitioner as defendant/opposite party No. 1 entered appearance in the said Election Tribunal Case by filing Written Statement, before the learned Election Tribunal below, denying material allegations raised in the aforesaid petition and stating that the said election of the Bashgari Union Parishad was held on 18-6-2011 without any objection, and all votes of the polling centres were sorted out and counted by the officers of the Election Commission in presence of the agents of all the contesting candidates. There are 9 (nine) polling centres and the dispute related to the polling centre for Ward No. 3, which was located at the aforesaid disputed polling centre. respondent No. 4 was the Presiding Officer and one Sukur Ali was the agent of respondent No. 3 for the aforesaid disputed polling centre; Respondent No. 4 as Presiding Officer declared the total casting votes of Chairman of the said Union Parishad without any objection and in presence of Presiding Officer, Polling Officer and the agents of the candidates and, as such, the agents of the candidates put their signatures on the Result Sheet without any objection. The Returning Officer declared the writ-petitioner (i.e., defendant/opposite-party No. 1 of the said Election Tribunal Case) as winning candidate who obtained a total of 2951 votes and, on the other hand, a total of 2928 votes were casted in favour of the respondent No. 3, who received second highest number of votes. On 3-8-2011, the Gazette was published by the Election Commission declaring the writ-petitioner, defendant/opposite-party No. 1 of the said Election Tribunal Case, as the Chairman of the said Union Parishad and, thereafter, oath was administered to the writ-petitioner.

7. On 23-1-2012, the defendant/opposite-party Nos. 4-10 of the said Election Tribunal Case also entered appearance by filing written statement, before the learned Election Tribunal below, denying allegations made in the petition of the said case.

8. At the time of trial of the said Election Tribunal Case before the learned Election Tribunal below, the respondent No. 3 as plaintiff/petitioner examined 3 (three) witnesses on 11-3-2012 and 16-4-2012 and, furthermore, adduced and marked some documents as Exhibit Nos. 1-12 to support his case and, conversely, the defendant/opposite parties examined 5 (five) witnesses on 9-5-2012 and 26-6-2012 to defend their case, as evident from the deposition of the witnesses.

9. In due course of the proceedings in the said election Tribunal Case, the respondent No. 3 as plaintiff/petitioner filed an application dated 29-7-2012 before the learned Election Tribunal below for recounting of votes at the aforesaid disputed polling centre, namely, Bashgari New Model High School under Ward No. 3 of the Bashgari Union, in view of the evidence as transpired from the deposition of the witnesses.

10. Upon hearing both the parties and perusal of the petition and written statements as well as deposition of the witnesses, the learned Election Tribunal below by Order No. 24 dated 17-9-2012 (Annexure-"E" to the writ petition) observed and came to the finding that, although the said date was initially fixed for pronouncement of judgment but prior to the passing of the final judgment in the said Election Tribunal Case, the order of re-counting of votes will be the most suitable and convenient way to ascertain the actual number of valid votes casted in favour of each of the candidates in the aforesaid disputed polling centre since the said Election Tribunal Case was filed challenging the legality of counting of votes. Accordingly, the learned Election Tribunal below by the said Order No. 24 dated 17-9-2012 directed the concerned authorities to open the gunny bag and re-count the ballot papers before the learned Tribunal in presence of the lawyers of both the parties on the next date.

11. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said order No. 24 dated 17-9-2012 passed by the learned Election Tribunal below, the petitioner filed a revisional application being Election Revision No. 23 of 2012 before the learned Election Appellate Tribunal and Court of District Judge, Narsingdi ("the learned Election Appellate Tribunal below"). Thereafter, upon hearing both the parties, and perusal of the petition, written statements, revisional application and deposition of the witnesses, the learned Election Appellate Tribunal below by the impugned judgment and order dated 8-1-2013 was pleased to reject the said Election Revisional Application on contest and, thereby, affirm and uphold the earlier Order No. 24 dated 17-9-2012 passed by the learned Election Tribunal below.

12. Thereafter, being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and Order dated 8-1-2013 (Annexure-"E-1" to the Writ Petition) passed by the learned Election Appellate Tribunal below, the petitioner moved this Court and obtained the instant Rule Nisi.

13. Respondent No. 3 entered appearance by filing Affidavit-in-Opposition. That case of respondent No. 3 is, inter alia, that:

The respondent No. 3 as plaintiff/petitioner filed the Petition of Election Tribunal Case No. 24 of 2011 stating that the respondent No. 3 along with others, including the petitioner, contested the aforesaid election for the post of Chairman of Bashgari Union Parishad, which was held on 18-6-2011. However, there were serious irregularities in counting the votes at the polling centre of Bashgari New Model High School for Ward No. 3 ("the aforesaid disputed polling centre"). Without taking into consideration the votes casted at the aforesaid disputed polling centre, the total number of votes casted at the remaining polling centres of the said Union Parishad in favour of the respondent No. 3 was 2665 (Two Thousand Six Hundred and Sixty Five), whereas the writ-petitioner obtained only 2330 (Two Thousand Three Hundred and Thirty) votes; thus respondent No. 3 was leading by 335 (Three Hundred and Thirty-Five) votes at the remaining polling centres, except the aforesaid disputed polling centre. Due to serious irregularities in the aforesaid disputed polling centre, the writ-petitioner was declared as chairman of the Bashgari Union Parishad by a margin of only 23 (Twenty-Three) votes, upon taking into account the votes of the aforesaid disputed polling centre. The final result sheet of the, said election showed that the petitioner obtained 2951 (Two Thousand Nine Hundred and Fifty-One) votes, whereas the respondent No. 3 obtained 2928 (Two Thousand Nine Hundred and Twenty-Eight) votes.

14. The respondent No. 4, who was acting as the Presiding Officer of the aforesaid disputed polling centre, illegally acted under the instruction and at the behest of the petitioner. Notwithstanding the objection raised by respondent No. 3, the concerned authorities failed to remove/transfer respondent No. 4 from the aforesaid disputed polling centre. On 18-6-2011, one personnel namely, Sukur Ali, who was appointed as polling agent of the respondent No. 3 at the aforesaid disputed polling centre, was about to leave the said polling centre at about 1530 hours for casting his own vote at another polling centre and, during that time, the respondent No. 4 deceptively made the said Sukur Ali sign the official result sheet of the aforesaid disputed polling centre in advance. Thereafter, when the said Sukur Ali, upon returning to the aforesaid disputed polling centre after casting his own vote at a different polling centre, noticed that the concerned authorities of the aforesaid disputed polling centre started counting the votes in his absence and, furthermore, discovered that 100 (One Hundred) invalid votes were illegally counted in favour of the petitioner, whereas only 17 (Seventeen) votes were recorded as invalid in the record of the election result of the said polling centre. The official result of the election purportedly showed that the petitioner obtained 621 (Six Hundred and Twenty-One) votes whereas the respondent No. 3 obtained 263 (Two Hundred and Sixty-Three) votes in the aforesaid disputed polling centre. The said Sukur Ali requested the concerned authorities to re-count the votes, but in vain.

15. Thereafter, respondent No. 3 submitted a letter dated 18-6-2011 before the Presiding Officer, respondent No. 4, for re-counting of total votes casted at the aforesaid disputed polling centre and, accordingly, the same was duly received by respondent No. 4. Furthermore, the respondent No. 3 raised concern in respect of the same before the Election Commission on 20-6-2011. It is pertinent to note here that the reports in respect of the aforesaid allegation were also reported in a number of daily national newspapers on different occasions. Notwithstanding the above, the Election Commission published a Gazette on 3-8-2011 declaring the petitioner as the Chairman of the Bashgari Union Parishad. Hence, the respondent No. 3 as plaintiff/petitioner filed the said Election Tribunal Case.

16. Mr Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing with learned Advocate Mr. Tushar Kanti Roy on behalf of the petitioner submits that both the learned Election Tribunal and Election Appellate Tribunal below failed to take into consideration the deposition of the witnesses. He further submits that neither the respondent No. 3 nor any other parties filed any application for re-counting of the votes however both the learned Election Tribunal and Election Appellate Tribunal below were pleased to direct the concerned authorities for re-counting of votes with malafide intention.

17. The learned Advocate for the petitioner next submits that the agents of the candidates did not raise any objection at the time of counting of the votes. He finally submits that respondent No. 3 did not file any application before the Presiding Officer on the day of election, i.e., on 18-6-2011, rather an application was made before the Returning Officer on the same day after pronouncement of result of the aforesaid election of Bashgari Union Parishad and, fur-there more, the ballot papers cannot be re-counted/inspected since the same are sacrosanct and, as such, both the Election Tribunals below overlooked the said vital aspect of the case.

18. Mr Mohammed Mutahar Hossain, the learned Advocate on behalf of the respondent No. 3, submits that the respondent No.1 as Presiding Officer of the aforesaid disputed polling centre failed to act in accordance with Rule 39(2) of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Election Rules, 2010 ("the Rules 2010") read with Section 5 of the Union Parishad Election Direction Mannual ("the Election Mannual"), notwithstanding the fact that the respondent No. 3 raised objection before the concerned authorities and requested for re-counting of votes at the aforesaid disputed polling centre since the respondent No. 4 failed to maintain its neutrality in the said election by acting in collusion with the petitioner so as to tamper the vote count. He next submits that the respondent No. 3 from the very outset, even prior to the election, by an application dated 12-6-2011 requested, amongst others, respondent No. 6 and 7 to change respondent No. 4 from the position of Presiding Officer of the aforesaid disputed polling centre since his neutrality is disputed by the petitioner as he acts at the behest of the petitioner. Mr. Hossain also submits that respondent No. 3 made an application dated 18-6-2011 before the Presiding Officer (i.e., respondent No. 4) for re-counting of total votes casted at the aforesaid disputed polling centre and, additionally, the respondent No.3 raised concern in respect of the same before the Election Commission on 20-6-2011 and, in this context, the aforesaid allegations are also reported in a number of daily national newspapers.

19. The learned Advocate for respondent No. 3 further submits that the respondent No. 3 is entitled to an order from the learned Election Tribunal and learned Election Appellate Tribunal below under Rule 62(1) of the Rules 2010 inasmuch as there is lack of transparency in counting of votes at the aforesaid disputed Polling Centre, as raised earlier by the respondent No. 3 before the respondent No. 4 on 13-6-2011, although the said fact was deliberately suppressed by the petitioner in the writ petition and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged for the interest of justice. Mr. Hossain also submits that the writ petition has been filed by the petitioner upon suppressing the material facts and misleading the Hon'ble Court inasmuch as it is abundantly clear that both the learned Election Tribunal and Election Appellate Tribunal below directed for recounting of votes upon perusing and assessing the deposition of witnesses and relevant evidence as well as on the basis of respondent No. 3's application dated 29-7-2012 and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged for the interest of justice.

20. Mr Hossain lastly contends that the impugned judgment and order dated 8-1-2013 and order dated 17-9-2012 passed by the learned Election Tribunal and Election Appellate Tribunal below are not amenable to judicial review under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh since the impugned judgment and orders were passed by a Civil Court under civil revisional jurisdiction and, as such, the present writ petition is not maintainable in its present form and manner.

21. Mr Hossain finally referred to several citations to substantiate his submissions, particularly, Abdul Qayum Sarder vs Rezaul Karim (Md), as reported in 47 DLR 241, Abdul Hamid Khan vs Miah Nurul Islam, as reported in 42 DLR (AD) 49, Moulana Abdul Matin vs Oli Ullah Khan, as reported in 42 DLR (AD) 76, Ansaruddin Ahmed vs Nasir Miah, as reported in 14 BLD (AD) (1994) 77 = 46 DLR (AD) 181, and 11C-81 Managing Director, Bangladesh Machine Tools Factory Ltd. vs Chairman, 2nd Labour Court, as reported in 44 DLR (AD) 272.

22. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the parties, perused the writ petition, its annexure and other relevant materials/exhibits on record, particularly, the petition, written statements and deposition of the witnesses of the said Election Tribunal Case along with the impugned judgment and order.

23. At this juncture it would be apposite to refer to the relevant provisions of the Rules 2010 and the election Manual, which, are relevant for the present writ petition. Rule 39(2) of the Rules 2010 provides that a Presiding Officer of a Polling Centre may recount the votes in his centre in the following circumstances, (a) if necessary, being self-spirited, or (b) if the contesting candidate or Election Agent or Polling Agent specifically submits written application in respect of the same and the same is found to be reasonable. Rule 62(1) of the Rules 2010 provides that both the Election Tribunal and Election Appellate Tribunal can pass order to open the gunny bags as well as ballot papers for its inspection. Furthermore, Rules 62(3) and 62(4) of the Rules 2010 provide provisions for ensuring that the secrecy of ballot papers is maintained. In this context, we are of the view that the fact that the ballot papers are sacrosanct does not prevent the Election Tribunal and Election Appellate Tribunal from exercising its power vested by Rules 62(3) and 62(4) of the Rules 2010 for inspecting the ballot papers and, thereby, recounting the votes. Furthermore, it is a well-established principle of law that the Election Tribunal has inherent power to direct for the recounting of votes. Rather, Rule 62 of the Rules 2010 now expressly grains, power to the Election Tribunals to inspect the ballot papers by opening the gunny bag and, furthermore, Rule 39(2) of the Rules 2010 allows the Election Tribunal to recount the votes for the stipulated reasons as provided by the said provision.

24. Section 5 of the Union Parishad Election Direction Manual ("the Election Manual") provides that a personnel and/or any teacher shall not be appointed as Presiding Officer if his/her role of neutrality is disputed by ethers. It appears that the respondent No. 3 has made out a prima facie case to question the neutrality of the Presiding Officer (i.e., respondent No. 4), however this Court would refrain from making any further observation on the said issue at this stage since the learned Election Tribunal below is yet to pass a final judgment on all the issues pending before it in the said Election Tribunal Case.

<u>25. Reverting back to the citations submitted on behalf of the respondent No. 3, it was held in Abdul Qayum Sarder vs Rezaul Karim (Md), as reported in 47 DLR 241, which was decided under the now repealed Union Parishad (Election) Rules, 1983 ("the Rules 1983"), that although there was no express provision for inspection of ballot papers and recounting of votes by the Election Tribunal under the Rules 1983 (now repealed), the Election Tribunal was still not barred from passing an order for re-counting in exercise of its inherent power. However, the election of the Union Parishads are now regulated by the Rules 2010 and, as such, it is abundantly clear that learned Election Tribunals below now have both express power under Rule 62 of the Rules 2010 as well as inherent power to pass an order of recounting of votes.</u>

26. It was further held in Ansaruddin Ahmed vs Nasir Miah, as reported in 14 BLD (AD) 77, the Election Tribunal is competent to order for recounting of the ballots when it finds that there exists a factual foundation for the same and it is necessary for a proper decision in the case.

27. Upon perusal of the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned Election Appellate Tribunal below and the impugned Order passed by the learned Election Tribunal below along with the deposition of the witnesses, it is palpably evident that both the learned Election Tribunal and Election Appellate Tribunal below came to a finding that there was factual basis for passing an order of inspection of ballot papers and re-counting of votes and, as such, we note that this Court under writ jurisdiction cannot interfere with such concurrent finding of the learned Election Tribunal and Election Appellate Tribunal below since the law allows the Election Tribunals to inspect ballot papers and recount votes in appropriate cases.

28. Furthermore, it is a well-established principle of law, as evident from Abdul Hamid Khan vs Miah Nurul Islam, as reported in 42 DLR (AD) 49 and Moulana Abdul Matin vs Oli Ullah Khan, as reported in 42 DLR (AD) 76, that the Hon'ble High Court Division shall not erroneously interfere with a disputed question of fact in writ jurisdiction and, as such, the present writ petition seeks to dwell on disputed question of facts and, hence, we refrain from entertaining any disputed factual issues raised before us. Also in Managing Director, Bangladesh Machine Tools Factory Ltd. vs Chairman, 2nd Labour Court as reported in 4 DLR (AD) 272, it was held that any appreciation or weighing or shifting of evidence is an issue of fact and a finding of fact is not reviewable in writ jurisdiction.

29. In view of the above discussions, made hereinabove, we do not find any merit in this Rule.

30. Accordingly, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

The earlier order of stay granted by this Court is hereby recalled and vacated.

End.

caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 54 of 1982
lawyer:
Mr. Akram Hossain Amin, with Mr. M. Golam  Rabbain, Advocates ------ for the Appellant. 
Mr. Mansur Habib, Advocate ------ for the Respondents.
parties:
Kamar Begum Roy ------ Appellant
Vs.
M. Khalilur Rahman ------ Respondent
case_source: Arising from the judgment and decree dated 28.1.82 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Additional Court, Rajshasi. in O. C. Suit No. 40 of 1978.
full_judgment:
Mohammad Ismail Uddin Sarker, J : This appeal by the defendant No. 1, Kamar Begum Roy (since deceased) is against the judgment and decree dated 28.1.82 passed by the Learned Subordinate Judge, Additional Court Rajshahi in O.C. Suit No. 40 of 1978, decreeing the suit.

2. The plaintiff-respondent No.1, M. Khalilur Rahman, instated O.C. Suit No. 198 of 1976 which was renumbered as O.C. Suit No. 40 of 1978 against the appellant and 9 others for declaration of his title simpliciter in the suit land measuring 23.18 acres described in the schedules Ka, Kha, Ga and Gha to the plaint on the allegations, inter-alia, that the suit properties originally belonged to Patia Four-Anna Raj Estate within the District of Rajshahi that the plaintiff used to serve as inspector of the said patia Four-Annas Estate; that the proprietor of  the said Patia 'Estate, Rani Sureswari Devi being satisfied  with the work of the plaintiff setteled the suit land with him on the 23rd of Aswin, 1354 B.S. at a total rental of Tk. 64/9/3 pies that since the pattan the plaintiff has been in possession of the suit land on payment of rent to the ex-landlord as well as to the Court of Wards on receipt of dakhilas that during the S.A. operation the suit land was recorded in the name of the ex-Landlord Rani Sureswari Devi in S.A . Khatian No. 97, 137, 138 and 142, that the plaintiff thereafter filed O.C. Suit Nos. 314/63, 261/63, 262/63, and 306/63 in the Court of Sadar Munsif, Rajshahi, against Rani Sureswari Devi in respect of the aforesaid Four Katians, that after the death of Rani Sureswari Devi her daughters were supporting the plaintiffs case but the plaintiff had to withdraw those suits later on in view of the provision of East Pakistan Ordinance No.1 of 1964; that the defendant No.1 filed a petition under section 50 of the State Acquistion and Tenancy Act before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Rajshahi claiming herself to be the wife of late Raja Naresh Narayan Roy being miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1964 and Miscellaneous Case No. 55 of 1965 to insert her name in the aforesaid four khatains after striking out the name of Rani Sureswari Devi therefrom and the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.) Rajshahi by his order dated 28.10.64 and 2.12.65 allowed the two miscellaneous cases directing to record the name of Rani Sureswari Devi from the four khatians, that the defendant No.1 was importer and she lost the case No.33 of 1950 before the Divisional Commissioner, Rajshahi and also before the Member, Board of Revenue in her attempt to register her name in the relevant touzis owned by the Patia four Anas Zaminder; that thereafter defendant No. 1 filed O.C. Suit No. 45 of 1951 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Rajshahi claiming her title in the properties of Patia four-anas Estate and she lost upto the Appellate Court, that Kumar Naresh Narayan Roy never married defendant No.1 and he never embraced Islam and he died as Hindu and his dead body was burnt according to Hindu custom; that the suit properties were enlisted as enemy properties by the Additional Deputy commissioner, Rajshahi and the Assistant Custodian of the enemy properties but on the ejection of the plaintiff the Asstt. Custodian released the properties in favour of the plaintiff; that there were many criminal cases between the plaintiff and the defendant No.1 wherein she admitted the title of the plaintiff; that the order passed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.). Rajshahi in Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1964 and 5 of 1965 under Section 50 of the State Acquistion and Tenancy Act substituting the name of defendant No.1 in place of Rani Sreswari Devi in the aforesaid S. A. khatians relating to the suit lands have cloud upon the title of the plaintiff over the suit lands and that the cause of action of the suit arose on 28.4.72 when the defendant No.1 claimed her title in the suit lands and hence this suit for simple declaration.

3. The appellant-defendant No.1 contested the suit denying the material averment made in the plaint and contending inter-alia, that the plaintiff had no cause of action for the suit; that the suit was not maintainable in its present form, the same being hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act; that the suit was barred by limitation; that the plaintiff never took settlement of the suit properties and if he produced any document in support of the so-called Patia Zaminder then all such documents were forged, spurious, fictitious and anti-dated; that it was not true that the defendant No. 1 was not married wife of Raja Naresh Narayan Roy alias Nuru Nabi Roy Chowdhury, that Raja Naresh Narayan Roy embraced Islam and adopted the name of Raja Nurun Nabi Roy Chowdhury and married defendant No. 1, that on the death of her husband the defendant inherited the suit properties and other properties left by her husband, that as Rani Sureswari Devi acquire no interest in the Suit properties the entry of her name in the S. A. Khatian was illegal and void that having no title and possession in the suit land the present suit of the plaintiff was liable to be dismissed.

4. The learned Subordinate Judge framed the following issues for determination in the suit:-

1. Is the suit maintainable in its present form?

2. Is the suit properly valued and stamped?

3. Is the suit barred by limitation?

4. Has the plaintiff alleged right, title and interest in the suit land, if so, is the plaintiff entitled to get a decree as prayed for?

5. To what relief, if any, is the plaintiff entitled?

5. At the trial the plaintiff examined eight witnesses including himself and produced certain documents in support of his case and the defendant also examined seven witnesses including herself and produced certain documents in support of her case. The learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit on the findings that the suit was not barred by limitation that the suit was maintainable in its present form and that the plaintiff has got title, interest and possession in the suit properties since his alleged pattan in 1354 B. S.

6. It is submitted by Mr. Akram Hossain Amin, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant that the learned Subordinate Judge was wrong in holding that the plaintiff took settlement in the suit land from Rani Sureswari Devi in view of the case of the plaintiff and the case he made out at the trial inasmuch as in plaint the plaintiff avert that he took settlement of the suit land by Dakhilas on the 23rd of Aswin, 1354 B. S. while in his deposition as P. W. 1 he stated that he took settlement of the suit land by virtue of four amalnamas and that the pattan was given to him in consideration of loan of Tk. 15,000/- to Rani Sureswari Devi. The learned Advocate has contended that the learned Subordinate Judge was wrong in finding that the plaintiff took settlement of the suit land from Rani Sureswari Devi on the basis of Exts. 18 to 18 (L). It is also submitted that the learned Subordinate Judge was wrong in not holding that the orders passed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.) in Miscellaneous case No. 9 of 1964 and 5 of 1965 under section 50 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act were set aside by the Divisional Commissioner and the Member, Board of Revenue. The learned Advocate further submitted that the learned Subordinate Judge was not correct in finding possession of the suit land with the plaintiff, without considering the evidence of the D.Ws.

7. Mr. Mansur Habib, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff—respondents on the other hand, has supported the judgment passed by the learned Subordinate Judge. The learned Advocate has contended that after the death of Raja Naresh Narayan Roy the defendant No. 1 tried to register her name in the touzis belonging to the patia Four-Annas Estate but she failed in view of Exts. 8 and 9 the orders passed by the Divisional commissioner, Rajshahi which was upheld by the Member, Board of Revenue. The learned Advocate has pointed out that in view of Exts. 14 and 14(A) the Gazette Notification acquiring the Four-Annas Patia Estate from Rani Sureswari Devi the learned Subordinate Judge was correct in holding that the plaintiff obtained settlement of the suit land from Rani Sureswari Devi. The learned Advocate for the respondents further submitted that the defendant failed to establish that Raja Naresh Narayan Roy embraced Islam or he married her and as such the appellant failed to prove that she acquired title in the suit land.

8. It may be mentioned at the very outset that the learned subordinate Judge neither discussed the oral evidence nor the documentary evidence adduced by the plaintiff and defendant No. 1 respectively. While considering the case of the plaintiff's title and possession the learned Subordinate Judge found as follows:

"It is said by the plaintiff that during S. A. operation, the land was recorded wrongly in the name of Rani Sureswari Devi. Against that record the plaintiff instituted four suits. That plaintiff actually filed four Title Suits against Rani Sureswari Devi relating to the suit property. Further, the plaintiff says that those suits were ended by Solenamas. Ext. 18-18(L) speak that the plaintiff took settlement of the suit property from Rani Sureswari Devi, wife of Raja Naresh Narayan Roy in 1354 B. S. All the P.Ws. Have deposed supporting the plaintiffs possession in the suit property since the date of the alleged pattan from Rani Srreswari Devi."

While considering the defendant's case the learned Subordinate Judge held as follows:-

"Ext. 8 and Ext. 9 show that the order in Misc. Case No. 9/64 and 5/65 U/S. 50 of the E. B. S. and T. Act by Addl. Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Rajshahi was set aside by the Commissioner and the Member, Board of Revenue. So in view of Ext. 8 and 9 it is found that the name of Rani Sureswari Devi was restored in S. A. Khatians of the suit property."

9. The above findings of the learned Subordinate Judge are not borne out by the evidence adduced in the case. It appears from the evidence that defendant No.1, Kamar Begum claims to be the married wife of Raja Naresh Narayan Roy since 17.10.41 and in support of her claim, apart from her oral evidence that Raja Naresh Narayan Roy embraced Islam and adopted the Muslim name of Nurun Nabi Roy Chowdhury on 17.10.41 and he married her on the same date she produced certified copy of a kabinnama dated 17.10.41 (Ext. A, the Kabinnama which was not included in the paper book); then according to her Raja Naresh Narayan Roy died on 23.9.43 as a Muslim leaving her as his sole heir. Then we find from the evidence that the defendant No. 1 filed suit No. 1508 of 1944 in the Original side of Calcutta High Court; Exts. 7 and 7(A) show that she instituted the suit for a declaration of her title to the property of deceased Naresh Narayan Roy on the basis of her marriage to him and conversion of her husband to Islam. That suit was dismissed for default on 1.9.49 in presence of the defendant. According to the appellant she came to Patia on 10.12.49 and entered into the palace of Raja of Patia for which there was a Criminal Case No. 569 of 1951 under sections 448, 148 and 380 of the Penal code in which she and the other co-accused were acquitted by the judgment dated 25.2.52, the certified copy of which has also been marked as Ext. A. Coming over to Patia she filed an application on 6.1.50 under section 42 of the Bengal Land Registration Act, 1876 praying for registration of her name in the land revenue register of Rajshahi Collectorate with respect to touzi No. 605 and some other touzis of Rajshahi Collectorate claiming inheritance from Raja Naresh Narayan Roy and the Land Registration Officer by his order dated 10.6.50 directed extra enquiry into the application of the appellant. Sureswari Devi then moved the Commissioner, Rajshahi Division invoking his interference and praying for quashing the proceeding before the land Registration Officer and the Commissioner, Rajshahi Division by his order dated 19.8.50 ordered that the proceeding be struck off (Ext.8) Against the order of the Divisional Commissioner, Rajshahi the appellant filed a revisional application before the Member, Board of Revenue who by the order dated 12.3.51 rejected her application confirming the order passed by the Divisional Commissioner, Rajshahi (Ext. 9).

10. The appellant thereafter filed O. C. Suit No. 45 of 1951 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Rajshahi against Sureswari Devi and others praying for declaration of her legal character and status as sole heir to the Patia Four Annas Estate left by Nurun Nabi Roy Chowdhury alias Kumar Naresh Narayan Roy of Patia. This suit was dismissed by the learned Subordinate Judge on the finding that the suit was barred under the provision of Order 9 Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure by the judgment and decree dated 11.6.58 (Exts. 10 and 11). An appeal was preferred by her being title appeal No. 11 of 1959 which was also dismissed by the learned District Judge, Rajshahi by his judgment dated 26.11.59 (Ext. 12). Then she filed S. A. No.62 of 1964 which was also dismissed by the High Court Division and the decision of the High Court Division was upheld by the Appellate Division on 11.6.81 in C. A.. No. 107 of 1980 holding that the suit was barred under the provision of Order 9 of Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

11. In the meantime the plaintiff-respondent instituted four suits in the Court of Sadar Munsif, Rajshahi being other suit No. 314/63, 261/63, 262/63 and 306/63 praying for declaration of his title in the suit land on the ground that the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of Rani Sureswari Devi in S. A. Khatians 97, 137, 138 and 142 on the allegation that he took settlement of the suit land on the 23rd of Aswin, 1354 B. S. from Rani Sureswari Devi but the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of Rani Sureswari Devi. It further appears that during the pendencey of those suits the plaintiff and Rani Sureswari Devi filed two petitions of compromise in O. C. Suit No. 314/63 and 261/63 and on the death of Sureswari Devi another set of petitions of compromise by the plaintiff-respondent and the daughters of Sureswari Devi were filed but the plaintiff ultimately withdrew both the suits on 23.11.65 on the ground that the suits were not maintainable without any prayer for consequential relief in the shape of confirmation of possession. So far as O. C. Suit Nos. 306/63 is concerned, both the suits were barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. It further appears that the plaintiff filed two appeals namely, Title Appeal No. S. 148 and 149 of 1965 against the order of dismissal of the latter two suits and at the appellants stage the plaintiff also filed two applications for withdrawal of the suits on the self same ground which were allowed (Exts. 4(G) and 4(H). It may be mentioned here that the plaint, the petition for compromise, the petition for adjournment etc. of O. C. suits 314/63 and 261/63 have been marked as Ext. 18 to 18(L).

12. The appellant, defendant No. 1 filed an application under section 50 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act which was numbered as Misc. Case No. 9 of 1964 praying for recording her name in S. A. khatian 97 in place of the name of Sureswari Devi and the Addl. Deputy commissioner (Rev.) Rajshahi by his order dated 28.10.64 allowed her application and directed to insert the name of Kamar Begum in S. A. kahtian 97 of mouza Patia in place of Sureswari Devi. Against this order of the Addl. Deputy Commissioner (Rev.) Rajshahi Panna Devi and 3 others, daughters of Sureswari Devi filed a petition for review which was rejected by the Addl. Deputy Commissioner, Rajshahi by his order dated 22.12.62 (Ext. B(1). Similarly the appellant filed another application under section 50 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, being Misc. Case No. 5 of 1965, for inserting her name in S. A. Khatians 137, 138 and 142 of mouza Patia in place of Sureswari Devi and this application was also allowed by the Addl. Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Rajshahi by his order dated 2.11.65 Accordingly the four S. A. Khatians were corrected in the name of the appellant.

13. Thus in view of the above discussions the finding of the learned Subordinate Judge that four O. C. suits were compromised now that the plaintiff took settlement of the suit land Rani Sureswari Devi as quoted earlier was wrong. Also the finding of the learned Subordinate Judge that the orders passed in Miscellaneous Case Nos. 9 of 1964 and 5 of 1965 were set aside by the Commissioner, Rajshahi Division and the Member, Board of Revenues restoring the name of Rani Sureswari Devi in the four S. A. khatians was wrong.

14. Now coming to the present suit, the plaintiff instituted the suit for declaration of his title simpliciter in the suit land without any prayer for consequential relief in the form of confirmation/recovery of possession of the self same allegation that he took settlement of the suit land from Rani Sureswari Devi. Although in the Plaint it has been stated that the plaintiff took settlement of the suit land from Rani Sureswari Devi by dakhilas dated 23rd Aswin, 1354 B. S. but in his deposition as P. W. 1 he stated that he took settlement of the suit land by four amalnamas and he filed the amalnamas Ext, 1 to 1(c), in support of his statement. He also alleged in the plaint that because of the promulgation of Disturb Persons (Rehabilitation) Ordinance, 1964 he had to withdraw the four O.C. suits filed in 1963; but as has been mentioned earlier the four O.C. suits were withdrawn on the ground that the suits for simple declaration without any preyer for consequential relief were not maintainable. In the present suit the plaintiff introduced the story of promulgation of Ordinance I of 1964 which provides that no suit for declaration of title be instituted or proceeded with without the permission of the authorised officer. The Plaintiff could have obtained the permission from the authorised officer and proceeded with those suits. It appears that the real difficulty was that the appellant by virtue of the orders passed in her favour in Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1964 and 5 of 1965 got her name inserted in the four khatians in place of Sureswari Devi and during the pendency of the above mentioned four O.C. suits she got herself added as defendant in the suits. That seems to be the real reason for the plaintiff to withdraw those suits.

15. The plaintiff has introduced another new story in his deposition stating that Rani Sureswari Devi took a loan of Tk. 15,000/- from him in consideration of which she granted settlement of the suit land in his favour. It appears from the evidence of P. W. 1 that he acted as an Inspector of the Patia four annas Estate although the defendant adduced evidence to show that the plaintiff was a Tashilder. He admitted in his cross-examination that 6/7 months after his appointment he took pattan of landlord 1½ months before he took settlement of the suit land. There is no evidence except the solitary statement of P. W. 1 in support of payment of loan to the Patia four-annas Estate. The alleged amalnama (Exts. to 1(C) are dated the 23rd Aswin, 1354 B. S. He has also filed dakhilas in support of his statement. Dakhaila Ext. 2(t) dated 23rd of Aswin, 1354 B. S. relates to the jama of Tk. 19/15/3 pie of the land of Ga, Gha schedule. The Dakhila Ext. 2(c) of 23rd Aswin. 1354 B.S. relates to the jama Tk. 25 and 7 annas in respect of Kha schedule land. The Dakhila Ext. 2(H) dated 5th of Kartik, 1354 B. S. relates to jama of Tk. 13/11 annas in respect of Ka schedule land and another Dakhila dated the 15th of Aswin, 1354 B. S. relates to the jama of Tk. 5/8 annas with respect to Gha shcedule land. Although the last mentioned Dakhila was filed in court but it was not marked as an Exhibit in the present Suit but it bears the mark of Ext. 1(c) of O. C. Suit No. 306 of 1969 and by this Dakhila the rent for the years 1351, 1352, 1353, 1354 was realised. The learned Subordinate Judge did not consider the four amalnamas but disposed of the suit by merely pointing out that Exts. 1 to 1(C) are the amalnamas and Ext. 2 to 2(W) are Dakhilas, without considering the defence that these were anti-dated and fraudulent papers created by the plaintiff for the purpose of the present suit. It is to be noted that the plaintiff did not mention about the amalnamas in his earlier suits nor even in the plaint of the present suit nor the plaintiff proved authority of person who granted the amalnamas as well as the Dakhilas. A very look at the 8 signatures in the four amalnamas by the alleged manager and Ammukhtar H. Chakraborty appears to be not in the same hand and seems to be forgery by limitation. In his deposition the plaintiff stated that the amalnamas were written by Shachindra Nath Datta and signed by Suresh Chandra, Manager and Anmukhtar of the Estate. It is not clear whether Suresh Chandra was H Chakraborty who purported to sign the four amalnamas. These amalnamas seem to be subsequently created as there was no mention about these amalnamas in the plaint as well as in the previous four O.C. suits of 1963. So far as the Dakhilas are concerned the two Dakhila Ext. 2(C) and 2(T) are of 23rd Aswin, 1354 B. S. and the Dakhila which was not exhibited is dated 15th of Kartik, 1354 B.S. This is contradictory to the plaint case and the statement of the plaintiff as P.W.1. Although the P.W.1 stated in his deposition that 13 Dakhilas were issed by Mohendra Nath Chowdhury and 9 Dakhilas were issued by B.D. Chandra Maitra, he took no step to prove that those persons were competent to grant those Dakhilas. So far as the payment of a loan of Tk. 15000/- by the plaintiff to Rani Sureswari Devi, this also appears to be an improvement introduced by the plaintiff at the trial of the suit. Firstly because this was not mentioned in the plaint and secondly because admittedly Rani Sureswari Devi used to reside in Calcutta and except the uncorroborated testimony of P.W. 1 there is no other material to show this new story of payment of loan.

<u>16. Now the question is whether Rani Sureswari Devi at all inherited the suit properties from Raja Naresh Narayan Roy and she was competent to grant the alleged settlement. As has been noticed earlier originally the suit land was recorded in the four S. A. khatians in the name of Rani Sureswari Devi. The appellant by obtaining orders of Addl. Deputy commissioner (Rev.), Rajshahi in Misc. Case No. 9 of 1964 and 5 of 1965 got her name inserted in those khatians in place of the name of Rani Sureswari Devi. The S.A. khatians were accordingly corrected and in the subsequent R.S. khatians the suit land was recorded in the name of the appellant. As the appellant got herself added as party defendant in O.C. Suit Nos. 314/63, 261/63, 262/63 and 306/63, the plaintiff had to withdraw those suits on the ground that the suit for simple declaration for title without any prayer for consequential relief were not maintainable. In the present case, apart from the plaintiff, there are seven other P.Ws. The plaintiff as P.W.1 stated about his possession in the suit land. P.W.2 Merajuddin stated that the plaintiff possessed the suit land for 14/15 years. He further stated that he came from India 15/15 years ago and admitted that he cannot say about the area the suit land. P.W.3 Abdul Majid stated that the plaintiff possessed the suit land. He also came to Patia from India 25/26 years ago and the suit land is 1½ miles away from his house. This P. W. 3 also stated that the defendant No. 1 was residing in the Kacharibari of the Estate, although the Judgment of the Criminal case which was also marked as Ext. A shows that the defendant No.1 was acquitted for trespassing into the house of Raja Naresh Narayan Roy in 1950 and P.W.1 admitted in his cross-examination that the house in which the defendant No.1 is residing now belonged to Raja Naresh Narayan Roy. P.W.4 stated that the plaintiff possessed the suit land for 20 years but admitted in his cross-examination that he has no land in Patia Mouza. P. W. 5 Kasimuddin stated that the plaintiff was possessing the suit land for 12/14 years. He also came from Murshidabad and admitted that he did not know about the area of the suit land. P.W.6 also came from Murshidabad. He also could not say the area and boundary of the suit land. P.Ws. 7 and 8 do not know about the suit land.</u>

<u>17. On the other hand, apart from the assertion of Kumar Begum as D.W.1 of her possession in the suit land and corrected S.A. Khatians and R.S. khatian. Ext. D series, she examined six D.Ws. in support of her possession. D.W. 2 Md. Alauddin Sarker worked as Moharer of Patia Estate and he knew the plaintiff who was a Tahsilder of Patia Raj Estate. He stated that the suit land situated surrounding the Rajbari in which the defendant No. 1 was residing since 1949. D.W.3 Kashem Ali was Peon of Paita Estate after the same was acquired by the Government. He stated that the plaintiff was a Tahsilder and defendant No.1 was possessing the suit land. In his cross-examination he further stated that he saw defendant No. 1 to catch fish from the tank. D.W. 4 Hafizur Rahman stated that his father was a Naib in the Four-annas Patia Estate. He stated that the defendant No.1 possessed the suit land. In his cross-examination he stated that he was Head Master of Buarida High School since 1973 and prior to that he was a teacher of Patia High School for six years. He seems to be a competent witness. D. W. 5 Md. Zaker Ali took lease of the tank by a registered lease deed from defendant No. 1. D.W.6 Samiruddin also took also lease of the tank from the defendant No. 1. The lease deeds were proved by them and marked as Ext. E. and E(1). D.W.7 Shajahan Ali also stated about the possession of defendant No.1. In his cross-examination he stated that he was a candidate in the last Parliament Election and sustained defeat, nevertheless he was a competent person. The learned Subordinate Judge did not sift the evidence of P.Ws and D.Ws. and jumped into the conclusion that "all the P.Ws. have deposed supporting the plaintiffs possession in the suit properties. "Upon an analysis of the oral and documentary evidence we find that plaintiff has failed to prove his possession in the suit land and consequently the suit was not maintainable in its present form being hit by the proviso to section 42 of the Specific Relief Act.</u>

18. It may be mentioned that the appellant filed the original Kabinama dated 17.10.41 in suit No. 150 of 1944 in the original jurisdiction of the Calcutta High Court. Although the suit was dismissed for default on 1.9.49 but on the prayer of the learned Advocate for the defendant of that suit, the learned Judge of Calcutta High Court directed the Registrar of Calcutta High Court to keep the Kabinnama in his custody. The appellant obtained the certified copy of the kabinnama from the Calcutta High Court and filed the same in the present suit which was marked as Ext. A. While deposing as D.W. 1 she stated "this is the certified copy of that Kabinnama" and in her cross-examination she denied the defence suggestion that the copy of the kabinnama was forged document. The certified copy of the kabinnama Ext. A shows that Kumar Naresh Narayan Roy embraced Islam on 17.10.41 and assumed the name of Nurun Nabi Roy chowdhury and on the same day after embracing Islam, he married the defendant No.1. It further appears from Ext. A that Nurun Nabi Roy Chowdhury alias Kumar Naresh Narayan Roy promised to pay the defendant a monthly allowance of Tk. 900/- and after her death half of the said amount towards the maintenance of her only daughter Rezina Zamal (who has been substituted in his appeal in her place after the death of defendant No. 1).

19. If there was conversion of Kumar Naresh Narayan Roy and his marriage with defendant No.1 and he had died as a Muslim, then Sureswari Devi did not inherit the properties of Naresh Narayan Roy. In this connection it may be pointed out that Mr. Mansur Habib, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-respondent has pointed out to us Ext. 14(a) the Gazette Notification dated 19.6.52 under Section 3(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and Ext. 14 the Gazette Notification dated 11.11.52 under Section 3(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act which show that the rent receiving interest and excess land was acquired by the Government from Rani Sureswari Devi, wife of late Naresh Narayan Roy of Patia. But these two Gazette Notifications relate to the rent receiving interest and non-retainable khas land of Rani Sureswari Devi. So far as the suit land is concerned. this was originally recorded in four S.A. khatians is the name of Rani Sureswari Devi but the Khatians were corrected pursuant to the orders passed by the Addl. Deputy Commissioner (Rev.) in Misc. Cases No. 9 of 1964 and 5 of 1965 and S.A. Khatians were corrected and subsequent R.S. Khatians were published in the name of defendant No. 11. In that view of the matter the plaintiff failed to establish that the suit land belonged to rani Sureshwari Devi from whom he claimed to have taken settlement. Thus, from the above discussions it appears to us that the plaintiff failed to establish his title and possession in the suit land; consequently the decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge cannot be sustained.

20. In the result, this appeal is allowed with costs and the suit is dismissed on contest against the contesting defendant with costs and ex-parte against the rest without costs.

End.
