full_judgment:
AFM Abdur Rahman J: Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009, Admiralty Suit No. 27 of 2009 and Admiralty Suit No. 28 of 2009, although have been heard separately one after another, yet the factual and legal aspect involved in these suits are similar, the same are now disposed of by this single judgment.

2. Fact of the suits in Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009. The plaintiff Kyung Hae Maritime Co. Ltd. of Korea instituted the Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009 against the vessel MV BF Glory ('ex-MV Kunai'), as defendant No. 1, Kysco, Shipping Co. Ltd., of Korea as principal-defendant No. 2, owners and parties interested of the vessel MV BF Glory; ('ex-MV Kunai') as principal-defendant No. 3, the Master of the vessel MV BF Glory as defendant No. 4 and Mariners Transport System Co. Ltd. of Bangladesh as principal-defendant No. 5 along with other proforma-defendants, praying for decree for realization of a sum of Bangladesh Taka 11,02,97,152.70 equivalent to US $ 15,90,442.76 to be realized from the principal-defendant jointly and severally.

3. The factual aspect of the plaintiff's claim inter alia is that the plaintiff is a company incorporated in South Korea and engaged in ship managing agent who in course of its business upon a negotiation made a ship management agreement with the defendant No. 2, the disponent owner/charterer regarding the vessel 'MV Tinai' and MV Kunai now renamed as MV BF Glory i.e. the defendant No. 1 vessel) for the purpose of marine operation, supply of bunkers, marine insurance, claims for seamen's wages and for repair and new building of the vessel and accordingly the plaintiff company supplied crews as per crew list to the defendant No. 1 vessel for which it was stipulated in the said ship management agreement that the owners shall remit the monthly management fee including seamen's wages to the bank account of the manager by telegraphic transfer. The plaintiff also supplied bunkers to the defendant No. 1 vessel through lubricants delivery receipt dated 19-10-2008 at the port of Pusan in Republic of Korea.

4. The plaintiff also supplied necessary items to the defendant No. 1 vessel on 14-10-2008 and also on other dates at the owners'/ master's disbursement. The plaintiff also completed electrical works to the defendant No. 1 vessel through POS Electric Engineering Company and supplied necessaries of electrical items as per list dated 23-10-2008 for the period of 7-10-2008 to 23-10-2008. The plaintiff also made services as per service report to the defendant No. 1 vessel by the order of the disponent owner/charterer the defendant No. 2, which commenced on 30-9-2008 and further on 16-10-2008 and completed on 23-10-2008. The plaintiff submitted the statement of account to the defendant No. 2 on different dates namely on 31-10-2008 for US $ 6,63,211.33, on 30-11-2008 for US $ 88,102.26, on 31-12-2008 for US $ 1,50,728.52, on 31-1-2009 for US $ 1,49,636.02, on 28-2-2009 for US $ 71,829.51, on 31-3-2009 for US $ 49,569.98 and on 30-4-2009 for US $ 44,187.24 totaling an amount of US $ 15,90,442.76. Although the plaintiff supplied the statement of accounts to the defendant No. 2, but the same is still outstanding for which the plaintiff is constrained to file the instant Suit finding the vessel within the territorial jurisdiction of this court.

5. It has been asserted in the plaint that the owner of the defendant No. 1 vessel wants to quit the BBC contract with the charterer defendant No. 2 as the charterer have not paid charter hire for more than three months. The owners defendant No. 3, asked the BBC charterer the defendant No. 2, to redeliver the vessel. As the defendant No. 2 i.e. the charterer is about to go bankruptcy, the plaintiff has no alternative but to institute the instant suit in Bangladesh to recovery their legitimate dues.

6. The Admiralty Suit 19 of 2003 was contested by the defendant Nos. 1 and 3 by filing written statement denying all the materials allegation of the plaint stating, inter alia, that Doosan Capital Co., Ltd. of South Korea is the owner of the vessel 'MV Tinai' and MV Kunai (now renamed as MV BF Glory the defendant No. 1 vessel) and the defendant No. 2 is Kysco, Shipping Co., Ltd. is not the owner of the defendant No. 1 vessel nor has any authority to enter into any agreement with the plaintiff for management of the vessel MV BF Glory. The defendant No. 2 is the lease user of the vessel and under article 27 of the lease agreement dated 27-5-2008, the defendant agreed to have no right to transfer the right of the vessel to the plaintiff without the owner's prior consent. The plaintiff with ill motive executed ship management agreement with the defendant No. 2 who is not the owner of the defendant No. 1 vessel and has no authority to transfer the right on the vessel and, as such, the owner of the vessel M/s Doosan Capital Co. Ltd. is not responsible for any liability in any manner under such unlawful agreement between the plaintiff and the defendant No. 2. Since the owner of the defendant No. 1 vessel has no connection, or any agreement with the plaintiff regarding the vessel or any supply of necessary or bunkers and the owner of the defendant No.-1 vessel never consented to transfer the right of such obtaining any supply or repair work from anybody, the owner of the vessel is not liable for any such payment. The plaintiff cannot carry out any service on the vessel without the order of the owner of the vessel as such any service allegedly rendered by the plaintiff to the vessel is unlawful and the owner is not liable for any such unlawful service.

7. It has been further asserted in the written statement that if there was any supply of crew members, spare parts, repairing work supply of bunker and any other services done to the vessel the same shall be business transactions in between the plaintiff and the defendant No. 1 and therefore the owner of the vessel is not responsible for such services as the plaintiff admittedly entered into an agreement with the defendant No. 2 who is not the owner of the vessel or had any authority to enter into any agreement with the plaintiff. The plaintiff may realize his alleged claim of US $ 15,90,442.76 from the defendant No. 2 Kysco, Shipping Co. Ltd., in personam and since the plaintiff is a Korean Company and the defendant No. 2 is also a Korean Company, the plaintiff with malafide intention did not institute suit in Korean jurisdiction. The owner of the vessel Doosan Capital Co. Ltd. never requested the plaintiff to do any job or made any supply in respect of the defendant No. 1 vessel and, as such, the owner of the vessel is not liable for the payment to the plaintiff. It has been categorically asserted that the plaintiff and the defendant No. 2 with ill motive created a fictitious ship management agreement dated 22nd September, 2008 knowing fully well that the defendant No. 2 had no authority to enter into such agreement. The plaintiff in order to make unlawful gain in collision with the defendant No. 2 created the ship management agreement dated 22 September, 2008. The defendant No. 2 is lease user of the vessel MV 'BF Glory under a lease agreement dated 27-5-2008 and under article 27 of the said lease agreement, the defendant No. 2 is prohibited from transfer arty right to the third party and therefore the suit is liable to be dismissed against the defendant No. 1 and 3.

8. Upon the aforesaid pleading of the par-ties this Court framed the issue to be adjudicated as follows:

1. Is the suit is maintainable under the admiralty jurisdiction in its present form and manner?

2. Is the suit is barred by the principles of limitation, estoppels, waiver and acquiescence?

3. Is there in ship manage agreement dated 22-9-2009?

4. Is there any cause of action against the defendant Nos. 1-3 for filing the instant suit?

5. Is the plaintiff is entitled to the relief as prayed for? or any other relief or reliefs granted to the plaintiff?

6. Is the defendant acknowledges receipt of the invoices for supply of necessaries and other services and settled such outstanding invoices?

9. In support of the plaint case the plaintiff examined one Mr Md Ahsanul Kabir, an Advocate of this Court, as a constituted attorney of the plaintiff as PW 1 while Mr Gujeong Song being the president of the plaintiff company was examined as PW 2.

The PW 1 exhibited the following documents:

Exhibit No. Identity of the documents.

1. 1(a) Power of Attorney dated 28-5-2009 and 16-3-2010

2. Fixture Notes

3. Bank slip dated 31-3-2009

4.5 Bank slip dated 7-4-2009 & 24-4-2009

6. Legal expenses on behalf of the owner

7. Invoice dated 12-5-2009

8.9 E-mail dated 11-5-2009 & 12-6-2009 .

10 Statement of delivery letter 2(a)(b), 6(a), 7(a) and 8(a)

Signatures.

10. On the other hand, the defendant Nos. 1 and 3 examined Mr Mehedi Hasan an Advocate of this court being the constituted attorney of the owner of the defendant No. 1 vessel as DW 1 who exhibited the following documents.

Exhibit No. Identity of the documents.

A. Certificate of Registry of vessel

B. Lease agreement dated 27-5-2008

C. Change of lease

D. Notice of default

11. Evidence of the plaintiff in Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009:

The PW 1 in his examination-in-chief stated that the plaintiff entered into the ship management agreement with the defendant No. 2 Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd, on 22-9-2008. The defendant No. 2 is the charterer and disponent owner of the defendant No. 1 vessel. As per the terms and condition of the agreement, the plaintiff is to manage the defendant No. 1 vessel and consequently authorised to make supply of bunker and all necessaries including supply of electrical goods payment of seamen's, wages, marine discharge and marine consultation and all kinds of incoming and outgoing services of the vessel. Accordingly, the plaintiff supplied bunkers, electrical goods made repairing of the vessel made payment of the seamen's, wages and also rendered other services in various ports including the port of Marcel in Korea from 1st October, 2008 till 30-4-2009. The plaintiff through various e-mail, sent to the defendant No. 2, requested for settlement of their claim, but the defendant No. 2 did not respond to the plaintiffs claim and therefore the plaintiff instituted the instant suit for realization of US $ 15,90,442.76 equivalent to Bangladesh Taka 11,02,97,152.70 against the defendant jointly and severally along with a prayer; for pendentility interest @ 20% per annum on the decretal amount. This PW denied the defendant case as to existence of any lease agreement with the defendant No. 2 by the owner of the vessel and also denied the claim of the defendant 1 and 3 that they are not liable to pay the claim amount of the plaintiff.

12. In his examination-in-cross the PW 1 stated that at the relevant time the defendant No. 2 Kysco, Shipping Co., Ltd. was in the possession of the defendant No. 1 vessel by virtue of an agreement dated 22-9-2008 as charterer and disponent owner of the vessel and the plaintiff entered into the ship management agreement with the defendant No. 2 Kysco, Shipping Co., Ltd., who was at that time the charterer of the vessel. This PW 1 admitted that there was no agreement in existence in between the plaintiff and defendant No. 3 and the plaintiff has got no, business relationship with the Doosan Capital Co. Ltd., and the defendant No. 2 Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. has already became a bankrupt. He further stated that the plaintiff has the claim against the defendant No. 2 and the other party as defendant in the suit. The PW 1 further stated that the master of the defendant No. 1 vessel placed the order and not the defendant Nos. 1 and 3 and that all these bills have been sent to the defendant No. 2 and not the defendant Nos. 1 and 3 the owner of he vessel and that the plaintiff has claim not only against the defendant No. 2 but against all the defendants.

13. The PW 2 Mr Gujeong Song stated in his examination-in-chief that the plaintiff company entered into a ship management agreement on 22-9-2008 with the defendant No. 2 Kysco Shipping Co., Ltd for the purpose of making all kinds of supply including bunker; marine insurance, supply of the seamen and their wages and repair. The plaintiff company supplied all kinds of supply to the defendant company in terms of the agreement for the period commencing from October, 2008 to April, 2009 and sent invoices, statement of accounts, debit notes and other documents along with the concerned receipt signed by the master of the defendant No. 1 vessel to the defendant No. 2. But the defendant No. 2 did not pay the dues so the suit filed by the plaintiff. This PW 2 proved the signature of the master and the chief engineer of defendant No. 1 the vessel on different receipt of documents.

14. In his examination-in-cross, the PW 2 stated that the defendant No. 2 Kysco Shipping Co., Ltd is not the owner of the vessel MV BP Glory and the said Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd., is now a bankrupt company. PW 2 admitted that the plaintiff has got no contract with the Doosan Capital Co. Ltd. or that no prior consent of Doosan Capital Co. Ltd., was taken prior to executing the ship management agreement with the defendant No. 2. This PW 2 further admitted that the plaintiff has an agreement with the Kysco Shipping Co., Ltd., and, as such, the plaintiff is asking money from the said company, the defendant No. 2, and also stated that although he has not filed any documents regarding the negotiation for three million with the owner of the vessel Doosan Capital Co. Ltd., yet the defendant Nos. 1 and 3 is liable to pay the claimed amount to the plaintiff.

15. Evidence of the defendant No. 1-3 in Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2008 On the other hand the DW J, Mr Mehdi Hasan in his examination-in-chief stated that the defendant No. 2 is not the owner of the defendant No. 1 vessel and the defendant Nos. 1 and 3 being owner of the defendant No. 1 vessel had no business relations with the plaintiff and that the defendant No. 2, charterer of the defendant No.1 vessel failed to pay the, hire money to the defendant Nos. 1 and 3 for more than three months and, as such, the owner of the vessel served termination notice upon the defendant No. 2, terminating the lease agreement, requesting return of the vessel to the defendant No. 3. The DW 1 further stated that there is a lease agreement between the defendant No. 2 and the owner of the vessel Doosan Capital Co. Ltd, the defendant No. 3, dated 27th May, 2008 Exhibit No, B and Article 27 of the said lease agreement prohibited the defendant No. 2 from transferring his right under the lease without prior consent of the owner to any third party. The ship management agreement as alleged by the plaintiff is a fictitious agreement only to gain unlawful profit.

16. In his examination-in-cross the DW 1 stated that he has filed power of Attorney on behalf of the defendant Nos. 1 and 3 in the office of this court when the application for release of the vessel was filed for which he could not exhibit the said power of Attorney which still remains in the office till the date of taking deposition.

17. Argument of the parties in Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2008 of the conclusion of the Evidence.

18. Although the, defendant has the right to summarize the case yet we have allowed the plaintiff to do so and accordingly while summarizing the entire case in Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009 before this Court, the learned Advocate Mr Kamal-ul-Alam appearing on behalf of the plaintiff, argued that the defendant No. 2 while admittedly a charterer of the defendant No. 1 vessel entered into the ship management agreement with the plaintiff for supply of the seamen and their wages, bunker, repair of the vessel etc. and accordingly the plaintiff supplied the agreed service to the defendant No. 1 vessel on the order of the defendant No. 2 and since the defendant No. 1 vessel received the necessaries and the service, the defendant No. 2 became liable for payment and accordingly the plaintiff served the required bill which has been exhibited before this court for a total amount of US $ 15,90,442.76. But as the defendant No. 2 failed to pay the said bill a maritime lien has been caused upon the vessel entitling the plaintiff to proceed in rem against the vessel as the vessel itself became primarily liable to pay for which the owner of the vessel is also liable in personam for the payment of the same. Since the instant maritime claim itself is a maritime lien making the vessel liable for payment and as the vessel would be sold for the purpose of satisfying its creditor, the question of contractual relationship with the owner of the vessel for the payment against the supply of the necessaries is immaterial. He strenuously argued that the supply of the necessaries and other service to the defendant No. 1 vessel was not denied by the defendant Nos. 1 and 3 and therefore the vessel itself or through the vessel the defendant No. 3 is liable to pay the dues to the plaintiff and on its failure the vessel would be sold in satisfying the decretal amount.

19. The learned Advocate Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, further argued that the supply of necessary and rendering service to the maritime vessel causes maritime lien upon the vessel itself and since the maritime lien runs with the res alike the order of injunction attached to the land and not against the party, therefore the res itself i.e. the defendant No. 1 vessel have been liable under the ship management agreement to pay the plaintiffs dues, in default the vessel will be sold in order to realize the decretal amount. In this respect the learned Advocate Mr Kamal-ul-Alam relied on the decision of an unreported case of this court in Admiralty Suit No. 37 of 1999 and also cases reported in 14 BLC 836, 310 US 268 and 2 LG 287.

20. The learned Advocate Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, argued that the plaintiff was not aware about any lease agreement regarding the defendant No. 1 vessel allegedly executed in between the defendant No. 2 and the owner of the vessel defendant No. 3 and, as such, not bound by of its any terms and condition and, as such, the defendant Nos. 1 and 3 cannot rely upon any prohibition as alleged in Article 27 of the said lease agreement. Moreover, the application of maritime lien cannot be prohibited under contract or agreement and the same will always run along with the res and, as such, irrespective of the existence of the alleged lease agreement the defendant No. 1 vessel will remain liable for all time to come till payment is made to the plaintiff for the supply of necessaries, bunker and other services.

21. The learned Advocate Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, finally argued that the defendant Nos. 1 and 3 failed to prove their alleged, claim stated in the written statement, since the DW 1 did not produce any lawful authority to depose before this court on behalf of the defendant No. 2 and since the DW. 1 has not obtained any valid power of Attorney from the defendant Nos. 1 and 3 nor did he depose as a witness upon having summons served from this Court. Moreover, the defendant Nos. 1 and 3 exhibited documents which being the photocopy, hit under section 65 of the Evidence Act, 1876 and, as such, cannot, be taken into consideration and therefore, the legal implication renders that the plaintiffs claim in the suit has not been controverted. Therefore, the plaintiff is entitled to the decree as prayed for.

22. On the other hand, the learned Advocate Mr AKM Fakrul Islam appearing on behalf of the defendant Nos. 1 and 3 argued that admittedly the defendant No. 2 is the charterer in possession of the defendant No. 1 vessel and the Doosan Capital Co., Ltd. is the registered owner of the defendant No. 2 vessel and at the relevant period a lease agreement dated 27-5-2008 was in existence in between the defendant No.1 and the said Doosan Capital Co. Ltd. regarding the long term lease of the defendant No. 1 vessel and under Article 27 of the said agreement the defendant No. 2 was debarred from transferring his right acquired under the agreement to any third party. But by violating the said clause the defendant No. 2 executed a ship management agreement with the plaintiff, obtained the supply of alleged seamens their wages, bunker, necessaries, repairs and other services for the defendant No. 1 vessel which however may be a liability of the defendant No. 2 but in no way made the registered owner Doosan Capital Co., Ltd. liable to pay the dues of the plaintiff.

23. The learned Advocate Mr AKM Fakrul Islam, strenuously argued that as the alleged supply of necessaries and services was made to the defendant No. 1 on the order of the charterer, the defendant No. 2, the defendant No. 2 is only liable and not the owner of the vessel liable in any way and, as such, no maritime lien can be treated attached to the defendant No. 1 vessel for the reason that maritime lien only accursed when the owner of the Res is liable to pay in personam for anything consumed by the res and fails to discharge his liability and only on that case a maritime lien attaches to his ownership vessel. But in the instant case, as the defendant No. 3 is not liable in personam to pay the dues of the plaintiff, no maritime lien can be attaches to his ownership vessel, the defendant No. 1 and, as such, this suit is not maintainable in rem though may be maintainable in personam against the defendant No. 2 Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. and therefore the suit is liable to be dismissed against the defendant Nos. 1 and 3.

24. The learned Advocate Mr AKM Fakrul Islam, further argued that the plaintiff cannot direct his claim against the defendant No. 1 or the registered owner of the defendant No. 1 vessel since the plaintiff made the alleged supply on the order place by the defendant No. 2 Kysco Shipping Co., Ltd., and since at the relevant period the master of the vessel was the employee of the defendant No.2 the charterer, the entire authority of the master to act shall be considered to have been derived from the charter i.e. the disponent owners, as such, the liability accrued from receiving such supply of necessaries goes to the shoulder of the defendant No. 2. Therefore the receipt and other documents issued by the master and the chief engineer of the defendant No. 1 vessel shall not be treated as made liable the registered owner of the vessel M/s Doosan Capital Co., Limited to pay the so-called dues of the plaintiff.

25. The learned Advocate Mr AKM Fakrul Islam, finally submits that the Power of Attorney appointing the DW 1 as an Attorney of the registered owner of the defendant No. 1 vessel, was filed in the registry of this Court along with the application for release of the vessel and although at the time of making deposition the original copy of the power of Attorney was not available, later the same has been brought from the court's registry and filed in the record prior to which a photocopy of the same was made exhibit, Therefore, the DW 1 had the authority to depose before this Court on behalf of the defendant Nos. 1 and 3. In this respect the learned Advocate Mr AKM Fakrul Islam, relied on the case reported in 55 DLR 471.

26. Refuting the argument of the learned Advocate Mr AKM Fakrul Islam, the learned Advocate Mr. Giasuddin Ahmed argued that the basic right under the agreement dated 27-5-2008 executed in between the defendant No. 3 and the defendant No. 2 was regarding the bareboat charter of the defendant No. 1 vessel and that had not transferred to the plaintiff by the defendant No. 2, rather only a ship management agreement was executed by the defendant No. 2 with the plaintiff which cannot be treated as transfer of the basic right under the said agreement and since the basic right of the defendant No. 2 under the said agreement dated 27-5-2008 is the lease hold right of the defendant No. 1 vessel, therefore in no way this can be termed as a transfer of the basic right. Accordingly, the learned Advocate Mr Giasuddin Ahmed argued the ship management agreement is not violative of the provision of Article 27 and Article 33 of the agreement dated 27-5-2008 executed in between the defendant Nos. 2 and the original owner of the vessel.

27. This is all about the agreements of the parties in Admiralty Smiralty Suit No. 28 of 2009.

28. FACTS IN ADMIRALTY SUIT No. 28 OF 2009

57. Issue No. 1: the maintainability aspect

This issue of maintainability of the action in rem so far it relates to Admiralty suit No. 19 of 2009 and 28 of 2009 has been seriously dealt with by the learned Advocate Mr Kamal-ul-Alam. According to the learned Advocate Mr Alam, the plaintiffs claim in Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009 since it involves realization of unpaid remuneration due on the basis of ship management agreement and for re-imbursement of the price for the supply of bunker, supply of necessaries and the cost of repairs made to the vessel and so far the claim raised in Admiralty Suit No. 28 of 2009 the same caused maritime lien upon the vessel and, as such, the action in rem against the vessel is maintainable, it is his further contention that the claim of the charterer ought to be taken as directed against the vessel itself causing maritime lien upon it and, as such, these two Admiralty suits being Admiralty suit No. 19 of 2009 and Admiralty Suit No. 28 of 2009, are maintainable as an action in rem under the provision of section 4 of the Admiralty Court Act, 2000 (Act 43 of 2000). His bone of contention is that three categories of situation is contemplated under section 4 of the Admiralty court Act. 2000, out of which the plaintiffs in these two Admiralty Suits relied upon the provision of section 4(2) and section 4(3) of the Act on the ground that the supply of bunker, necessaries and cost for repair creates maritime lien upon the vessel itself and, as such, the vessel itself became liable for payment of the maritime claim, since the maritime lien traces with the res alike the order of injunction attached to the land and not against the party.

The learned Advocate Mr Kamal-ul-Alam made out a case that although the registered owner of the vessel relied upon the so-called lease agreement dated 27-5-2008 and a prohibition under Article 27 and 30 of the same, yet it shall have no implication against the actual attachment of maritime lien upon, the vessel on the ground that the Maritime lien cannot be prohibited to be attached to the vessel by contractual agreement and moreso that the said lease agreement has not been proved before this court through a competent witness. 68. Section 4 of the Admiralty Court Act, 2000 with its sub-section provide as follows;

Admiralty Court Act, 2000

Section 4—Mode of exercise of admiralty jurisdiction—(1) Subject to the provisions of section 5, the admiralty jurisdiction of the High Court Division may in all cases be exercised in personam.

(2) The Admiralty Jurisdiction of the High Court Division as the Court of Admiralty may in the cases of claims mentioned in clauses (a) to (c)and (r) of Sub-section (2) of section 3 be exercised in rem against the property in question.

(3) In any case where the amount claimed relates to any ship, aircraft or other property over which there is a maritime lien or other charge, the Admiralty Jurisdiction of the High Court Divisions as the Court of Admiralty may in such a case be exercised by an action in rem against that ship, aircraft or property.

(4) In the case of any such claim as is mentioned in clauses (d) to (q) of subsection 2 of section 3 of the Act, being a claim arising in connection with a ship, where the person who would be liable on the claim in an action in personam was, when the cause of action arose, the owner or charterer of, or in possession or in control of, the ship, the Admiralty jurisdiction of the High court Division as the Court of Admiralty may (whether the claim gives rise to a maritime lien on the ship or not) by invoked by an action in rem against the following ships, namely-(a) if at the time when section is brought, the person has beneficial ownership over all the shares of the ship; or (b) if any other ship which, at the time when action is brought, is under the beneficial ownership of the person as aforesaid.

69. In view of the aforesaid provisions, it appears that the question of attachment of maritime lien upon a maritime vessel has a vital implication of the maintainability of a suit as an action in rem.

70. The plaintiffs claim for price of bunker, necessaries and the cost of repairs and also ship management fees in Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009 and also charterer expenses in Admiralty Suit No. 28 of 2009 are undoubtedly claim against the other party engaged in maritime business to be termed as maritime claim but whether such maritime claim attached any 'maritime lien' upon the vessel MV BF Glory has to be considered by this court on the general meaning of lien as considered in all the legal jurisdiction of the whole world.

71. CARVER, the celebrated author in admiralty matter, defined lien as a privileged charge upon a property in order to secure the payment of a legitimate claim. The Chambers Dictionary defined lien as a right to retain possession of another's property until the owner pays a debt or fulfils a contract.

72. The question of attachment of maritime lien on the res has been considered in many cases in the common law jurisdiction. In THE CASTLEGAT I reported in 1893 AC 38 Lord Watson observed that "a proper maritime lien must have its root in the personal liability of the owner".

73. In the case of THE BOLD BUCCLEGGH, sir John Jervies provided the first comprehensive and authoritative definition of maritime lien in the following language;

"........A. maritime lien is well defined...to mean a claim or privilege upon a thing to be carried into effect by legal process that process to be a proceeding in rem this claim of privilege travels with the thing in to whosever possession it may come. It is in ckohet from the moment the claim or privilege attaches, and when carried into effect by legal process by a proceeding in rem, relates back to the period when it first attached"

<u>74. Therefore, it appears that a maritime lien will arise when owner of maritime vessel incurs debt for which he is personally liable and defaults in repaying the debt a charge is immediately created and automatically attached to his property i.e. the vessel as a security for re-payment. Therefore, a maritime claim may be turned into a maritime lien to be attached to the maritime res if the claim arises against the owner of that particular maritime res in personam. But a long practice in maritime jurisprudence have classified the charges, which only creates maritime lien.</u>

75. The celebrated author Dr Thomas in his British shipping laws writes that—

"currently following claims have been recognized as creating maritime lien:

a) Damage done to ship

b) Salvage

c) Seaman's wages

d) Master's wages & disbursements

e) Battomry and Respondtia".

76. There appears no, other maritime claim as identified as creating maritime lien upon the vessel neither in the common law jurisdiction or elsewhere.

77. Doosan Capital Co. Limited is the admitted registered owner of the vessel MV BF Glory. In paragraph No. 3 of the plaint in the Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009 the plaintiff asserted that after negotiation the plaintiff made a ship management agreement with the deponent owner/charterer, the defendant No. 2 on 22-9-2008 regarding the vessel 'MV Tinai' and MV  Kunai (now renamed as MV BF Glory i.e. the defendant No. 1 vessel. In paragraph No. 3 of the plaint in Admiralty Suit No. 28 of 2009 the plaintiff stated that it has acted as voyage charterer of the defendant No. 1 vessel by virtue of charter party (fixture note) agreement dated 2-3-2009 and 19-3-2009 with BF Shipping Company (as owner of the defendant No. 1 vessel MV BF Glory ex-MV Kunai). The vessel MV BF Glory and the owner of the vessel M/s Doosan Capital Co. Limited in their written statement asserted that the M/s Doosan Capital Co. Limited is the original owner of the vessel MV BF Glory and under a lease agreement dated 27-5-2008 the possession of the vessel MV BF Glory was handed over to the lease user M/s Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. Upon such factu al aspect the DW 1 in both the Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009 and Admiralty Suit No. 28 of 2009 stated in his deposition that M/s Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd., is the lease user of the vessel MV BF Glory. This DW 1 also exhibited the lease agreement as exhibit-B who has been heavily assailed by the learned Advocate Mr Kamal-ul-Alam on the ground that no authority of the DW 1 has been filed to this Court to depose and the Exhibit-B being photocopy of the documents, allegedly to be a lease agreement, cannot be taken into consideration by this Court.

78. It appears that the DW 1 denied this suggestion that he has not filed the power executed by the M/s Doosan Capital Co. Limited in his favour to depose in these suits, rather he has asserted that the power in original has been filed in the registry of this Court along with the application for release of the vessel MV BF Glory and the learned Advocate Mr. AKM Fakrul Islam by an application prayed for bringing the original copy of the power from the office although he has made a photocopy of the said power as exhibit for which we have brought the power from the registry wherefrom it appears that the DW 1 has been engaged by the M/s Doosan Capital Co. Limited to depose in these suits. Therefore, the argument of the learned Advocate Mr Kamal-ul-Alam assailing the authority of DW 1 to depose has no merit to be considered by this Court.

79. It further appears that the exhibit-B, although a photocopy of the lease agreement, executed in between the owner of the vessel MV BF Glory, M/s Doosan Capital Co. Limited and the lease user M/s Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. has been admitted by the plaintiff that the defendant No. 2 was the disponent owner as charterer of the vessel MV BF Glory in the plaint of the Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009. Therefore, this assertion proved by admission that the defendant No. 2 M/s Kisco Shipping Lines Limited, in Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009, is not the original owner of the vessel MV BF Glory ('ex-MV Kunai').

80. Therefore it is now to ascertain whether this deponent owner M/s Kysco Shipping Lines Ltd. had the authority to enter into ship management agreement with the plaintiff.

81. In this respect the PW 2, the president of the plaintiff's company in his examination- in-chief, categorically stated that the plaintiff's company entered into a ship management agreement on 22nd September, 2008 with the defendant No. 2 M/s Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. for managing the defendant No. 1 vessel, making all kinds of supply including bunkers, marine insurance, supply of the seamen and their wages and repair and all these supplies were made to the defendant company the period commencing from 28th October, 2009. This PW 2 exhibited the ship management agreement as exhibit No. 2 and he proved the signature of the defendant No. 2 M/s Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd., upon the said agreement.

82. The DW 1 in this respect stated that the Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. made the exhibit-2 unauthorised since the Article 27 of the lease agreement prohibited such an agreement to be executed by the lease users. But the learned Advocate Mr Giasuddin Ahmed, appearing on behalf of the plaintiff in Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009 and 28 of 2009, categorically asserted that Article 27 of the lease agreement reveals that the basic right of the lease user cannot be transferred to a third party and since the basic rights involved the leasehold right of the Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. to use the vessel the same cannot be transferred under the prohibition of Article 27 of the lease agreement. But since the Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. has only made the ship management agreement, the same will not come under the preview of the prohibition as made in Article 27 of the lease agreement dated 27-5-2008.

83. Upon examination of Article 27 of the lease agreement, Exhibit-B, it appears that these stipulated a restriction in the provision against the transferability of the rights of the lease user to any 3rd party. But the question involved here is not regarding the prohibition, rather the question involves whether the claim for the price of bunker and necessaries, the cost of ship management and the cost of repairs as allegedly incurred by the plaintiff can be directed against the original owner of the vessel when the vessel was under the deponent owner as charterer who admittedly received the said services.

84. It further appears from exhibit- 3, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 and 16 in Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009, which are statement of accounts submitted to the defendant No. 2 the Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. so also the exhibit-5 series being the receipt invoice and delivery note to the defendant No. 2 Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd., that the master of the defendant No. 1 vessel and the Chief Engineer received the supply as alleged. The PW 2 proved the signature of the master of the vessel and the engineer on exhibit-5 series which are marked as exhibit-7 series. Therefore question arises as to the authority of the Master whether he has received the service and the bunker, as supplied by the plaintiff, under the authority of the original owner or the admitted deponent owner/charterer of the vessel?

85. It appears that at the relevant period admittedly the vessel was under the lease agreement with M/s Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd., the defendant No. 2, under which the entire control and possession of the vessel was transferred to the defendant No. 2 Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. A lease of a vessel for specific period has the implication as bareboat charter party upon which the full possession and control of the vessel and its crew member including the master goes to the lessee and in that case the master of the vessel derives authority from the lessee and not from the original owner. In this respect, we can profitably consider the decision in the case of Marine Oil Broking Company Pte Ltd. vs Daizu Maru reported in 55 DLR 471 as referred by the learned Advocate Mr Kamal-ul-Alam wherein their lordship in this Court on a similar point held as under;

"Had it been proved on a preponderance of evidence that the bunkers were supplied on the orders made for and on behalf of the owners of Daizu Maru, in that case, the plaintiff would be able to maintain an action in rem against the vessel, otherwise not"

86. In the aforesaid case, a similar cause arose as to who is liable for payment of bunker price when the vessel MV Daizu Maru was under time charter with the defendant. This decision is well founded and there is no reason to disagree with the position mentioned therein. Because the maritime lien accrues as only as security for payment for a debt of a person or company and only against the property of the creditor. In the instant case, it appears that the claim of the plaintiff being a debt is squarely against the defendant No. 2 M/s Kysco, Shipping Co. Ltd., which will create maritime lien upon their ownership vessel and not upon a vessel upon which they have only a lease hold interest for a definite period.

87. In Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009 and Admiralty Suit No. 28 of 2009 since the defendant No. 2 admittedly not the real owner rather the deponent owner, particularly under a lease agreement, the debt incurred by it cannot create a lien upon the property not owned by it. The vessel MV BF Glory being the property of real owner of M/s Doosan Capital Co. Limited cannot be liable for the debt created by the lease user of the vessel, liability of which always remains with the said company M/s Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. Therefore, this court finds that the maritime claim of the plaintiff in respect of the ship management fee price of bunker, and necessaries and cost of repair of the vessel could not cause maritime lien upon the vessel MV BF Glory and, as such, cannot be realized in admiralty jurisdiction through an action in rem and therefore the claim of the plaintiff against the res as an action in rem cannot be maintained neither against the vessel itself nor the real owner of the vessel M/s Doosan Capital Co. Limited.

88. But does that mean the plaintiffs claim will be frustrated against M/s Kysco Shipping Lines Ltd. as it went to bankruptcy. The answer is empathic 'No'.

89. It appears that the plaintiff rendered service in favour of the said Kysco shipping Lines Ltd. under the ship management agreement, supplied the bunker to the vessel and necessaries and also rendered service in respect of the repair of the vessel under the authority of the defendant No. 2 Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. and therefore the defendant No. 2 is liable to pay the price due to the plaintiff. Accordingly, the instant proceeding in Admiralty Suit No. 28 of 2009 is maintainable as an action in personam against the said defendant No. 2 company M/s Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. and also against the BF Shipping Company Limited who was the later lease user of the vessel at the relevant time. Therefore, the issue No. 1 as to the maintainability of the suit is disposed of in favour of the plaintiff, albeit, only as an action in personam against the defendant No. 2 M/s Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd., in Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009 and against the BF Shipping Company Limited in Admiralty Suit No. 28 of 2009.

90. Admiralty Suit No. 27 of 2009 has also be alleged to have been initiated as an action in rem. In this suit, the plaintiff raised claim for the price of bunker against the vessel MV BF Glory on the different fact that not only bunker has been supplied to the vessel MV BF Glory when the same was named as MV Kunai, but also to the sister vessel 'MV Tinai' (now MV BF Hope) during the period of 14th March, 2009 at Fujeria United Arab Emirates. The DW 1 stated in his evidence that the vessel was under the lease hold use of the said Kysco Shipping Co, Ltd, at the relevant date 14th March, 2009. As the court has already held elsewhere in this judgment that the supply of bunker to the vessel MV Glory and received by the master of the said vessel since it did not confer any maritime lien upon the vessel, the instant proceeding in Admiralty Suit No. 27 of 2009 to realize unpaid bunker price from the owner of the vessel for both the vessel also is not maintainable as an action in rem but maintainable as an action in personam against the charterer and parties interested in the vessel MV BF Glory the defendant No. 4 the registered owner of the vessel Doosan Capital Co. Limited the defendant No. 3 is not liable for the payment of the price of bunker as supplied by the plaintiff to the vessel which is a undoubted liability of the charterer. Therefore, the Issue No. 1 in respect of Admiralty Suit No. 27 of 2009 is disposed of in favour of the plaintiff only to the extent that the instant suit is maintainable in personam against the defendant No. 4 Charterer and parties interested the vessel MV BF Glory.

91. Issue No. 2 the cause of action aspect:

PW 2 in Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009 and Admiralty Suit No. 28 of 2009 proved the statement of accounts and the receipt of invoice by the master of the vessel MV BF Glory in respect of the supply of bunker and also invoices of the ship management fee along with the bill for the repair, the supply of seamen's and their wages against which no dispute has been made by the contesting defendant, rather it has been admitted by the defendant Nos. 1 and 3 that since the defendant No. 2 Kysco, Shipping Co., Ltd., and the BF Shipping Limited at their respective lease period obtained the service and the supply of bunker and necessaries, the said defendant No. 2 is liable to pay the dues of the plaintiff. This court finds substance in the contention and hold findings that the plaintiff successfully proved the cause of action of the suit against the defendant No. 2 Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. and the BF Shipping Ltd. so far the claim as made in Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009 and Admiralty Suit No. 28 of 2009 is concerned.

92. It appears that in Admiralty suit No. 27 of 2009 bunker was also supplied on 14th March, 2009 to the vessel MV BF Glory while the same was named as MV Kunai but the said vessel MV Kunai was at that time was on lease to BF Shipping Limited "and therefore the BF Shipping Limited is liable to pay the price of the bunker to the plaintiff as receipt by the master of the vessel under the exhibits, made before this court, are the acknowledgment of the receipt of the bunker delivery.

93. But in Admiralty Suit No. 27 of 2009 although a further claim was raised in respect of supply of bunker to 'MV Tinai on 7th March, 2009, but no cogent evidence has been adduced by the plaintiff in this suit in respect of supply of bunker to the vessel 'MV Tinai' when the same vessel allegedly to have been under the possession of the concerned lessee BF Shipping Limited. Therefore, the claim against the 'MV Tinai' not being proved before this Court cannot entertain the same and finds that the so far the question of payment of bunker price is concerned regarding the MV BF Glory ('ex-MV Kunai'), the plaintiff of Admiralty Suit No. 27 of 2009 successfully proved the cause of action against the BF Shipping Limited. Therefore, this issue is disposed of in favour of the plaintiff of the aforesaid three suits and against the defendant Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. and BF Shipping Limited.

94. Issue No. 3 the liability aspect:

The defendant No. 2 in Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009, the Kysco shipping Lines Limited opted not to contest the suit although the notice has been properly served upon their local agent, defendant No. 5 Mariners Transport System Company, 67 Agrabad Commercial Area, Chittagong, so also the owners and parties interested in the vessel MV BF Glory did not contest the suit despite the fact that the notice of the suit has been served with notice of the suit duly their local agent M/s Atlas Shipping Agency, 31, Agrabad Commercial Area, Chittagong.

95. In Admiralty Suit No. 27 of 2009 the defendant No. 4 Charterer and parties interested in the vessel MV BF Glory also opted not to contest the suit although the local agent of the Charterer and parties interested in the vessel M/s Mariners Transport System Company Limited has been served with notice of the suit duly. Therefore all the suits have proceeded ex parte against the aforesaid defendants. The exhibited documents in the aforesaid suit, the corroborating evidence of PWs has clearly proved that the lease user of the vessel MV BF Glory ('ex-MV Kunai') since received the service, bunkers, necessaries and the repairs of the vessel are liable to pay the price and cost of the same to the plaintiff. Therefore, as the plaintiff could successfully prove the cause of action against the said defendant as liable in personam, decree is required to be passed against the said defendant in favour of the plaintiff for realization of the amount as claimed in the suit. Therefore, this issue is disposed of in favour of the plaintiff and against the aforesaid defendant.

96. Issue No. 4: aspect of further relief or reliefs to the plaintiff.

It appears from the evidence on record that the defendant No. 2 in Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009 Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. is either about to be bankrupt or in the meantime became bankrupt. But the status of the other defendant i.e. the BF Shipping Ltd. has not been clarified by any cogent evidence before this Court. Therefore, this Court finds that the decree to be passed in the suit against the Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. will be executable against the asset of the said company, the defendant No. 2 Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. if the same has already gone into liquidation, as a secured debt of the plaintiff. Therefore, this Court finds that if the said company Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. already liquidated the decree passed against it shall stand against the available assets in the hands of the liquidator with a priority in payment. Therefore, this Issue is disposed of in favour of the plaintiff against the aforesaid defendant.

97. As all the Issues have been disposed of in favour of the plaintiff, these three suits is required to be decreed in favour of the plaintiff not to the strict sense of the prayer but in modified form.

The Court fee paid is sufficient.

98. Hence, ordered.

Let a decree be and hereby passed in Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009 for realization of an amount of US $ 15,90,442.76 (equivalent to Bangladesh Taka 11,02,97,152.70) along with interest pendentility @ 20% of the decreetal amount from the date of filing of the suit and also the cost of suits against the defendant No. 2 Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. and the suit is dismissed against the defendant Nos. 1, 3 and 4 and also decreed in Admiralty Suit No. 28 of 2009 against the BF Shipping Limited, Parties and interested in the vessel MV BF Glory ('ex-MV Kunai') for realization of an amount of US $ 80,561 (equivalent to Bangladesh Taka 55,86,905.35) along with interest pendentility @ 20% till the actual realization of the decreetal amount and also the cost of the suit. Further it is hereby decreed in Admiralty Suit No. 27 of 2009 against the defendant No. 4 charterer and parties interested in the vessel MV BF Glory being BF Shipping Limited for realization of an amount of US $ 1,47,917.32 (equivalent to Bangladesh Taka 1,01,32,336.42) along with interest pendentility @ 20% and the cost of the suit and the suit is dismissed against the defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 3.

All the amount decreed will be treated as liquidated debt against the defendant No. 2 in Admiralty Suit No. 19 of 2009 M/s Kysco Shipping Co. Ltd. and also against the BF. Shipping Limited in Admiralty Suit No. 27 of 2009 and Admiralty Suit No. 28 of 2009.

End.
