full_judgment:
Md. Mozammel Hoque, J: This First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 44 of 1999 has been preferred by Mr. Md. Emdadul Haque and First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 67 of 1999 had been preferred by Mr. Md. Ataur Rahman Khan. Both the appeals have been preferred against the judgment dated 24.01.1999 passed by Elation Case No. 13 of 1997. Since both the appeals have arisen out of the judgment passed in Election Case No. 13 of 1997. and since in both the appeals the parties as well as the points of determination are identical, they were heard together and are being disposed of by one judgment.

2. Facts stated below will cover both the appeals. Md. Ataur Rahman Khan was the election petitioner in the Election Petition it was stated in short that election petitioner Md. Ataur Rahman Khan contested the election of last Jatiyo Sangshad Election held on 12.06.1996 from constituency No. 203, Narayangonj-2. Election Petition was filed against Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan and 5 others who contested the election in the above constituency against the election petitioner. Appellant Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan contested the election with "Boat" Symbol and election petitioner Md Ataur Rahman Khan contested the election with "Sheaf of Paddy" Symbol. There were 69 election centres (polling stations) out of which the results of 63 polling stations were declared and election of 6 centres was postponed. Again on 19.06.1996 election in the aforesaid 6 election centres was held and thereafter the Returning Officer votes and declared the result of aforesaid 6 election centres was held and thereafter the Returning Officer counted the votes and declared the result of the election showing Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan having "Boat Symbol" obtained 58,947 votes and election petitioner Md. Ataur Rahman Khan having "Sheaf of Paddy Symbol" obtained 58,388 votes and thereby declared Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan as elected Member of Parliament from the aforesaid Constituency by a margin of 559 votes. Being defeated the election petitioner (having Sheaf of Paddy Symbol) Md. Ataur Rahman Khan Med the election petition before the Election Tribunal.

3. It is alleged in the election petition that on 12.06.1996 the polling agents of the election petitioner is Shambupura, Domar Char and Khaliar Char election centres were driven out by the people of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan and the supporters of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan in collusion with the Presiding Officer and the Assistant Presiding Officer were rigging the votes in favour of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan. Out of fear the polling agents of election petitioner could not dare to make any protest. On 19.06.96 in the re-election of Shatgram election centre, there was randam rigging and the agent of the election petitioner Mostatizur Rahman raised protest to the Presiding Officer but without any result. In that election 229 voters of Charigoan village were not allowed to come to the polling centre and to that effect one Israfil raised protest to the Assistant Presiding Officer but without any result.

4. In Shambupura election centre Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan got 1740 votes out of total 1909 votes cast and election petitioner got zero vote. In Domar Char election centre out of total 2541 votes, 2190 votes were cast and Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan got 2172 votes and election petitioner got zero Vote. In Khaliar Char centre out of 2147 votes, 1647 votes were shown cast and Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan got 1348 votes were shown cast and Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan got 1348 votes and election petitioner got 289 votes. In Shatgram election centres out of 3393 votes, 2651 votes were shown cast and Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan got 2167 votes and election petitioner got 438 votes. If the ballot papers and other election materials were called for examination, it would be found that there was unprecedented rigging in the election and if the invalid votes were deducted from the count of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan the election petitioner would definitely be elected as Member of Parliament from the above Constituency by a big margin.

5. Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan, the respondent No. 1 in the Election Petition and appellant in First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 44 of 1999 contested the election case by filing written objection and denied all the allegations made by the election petitioner Md. Ataur Rahman Khan. In his written objection he stated that in the election held on 12.06.1996 there were disturbances in 6 election centres and peaceful election was held in 63 election centres. In 6 election centres the re-election was held on 19.06.1996. In 63 election centres the election petitioner got 53,251 votes and opposite party No. 1 appellant Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan got 49,802 votes and thereby the election petitioner Md. Ataur Rahman Khan was leading by a margin of 3,449 votes before the re-election was held in 6 centres on 19.06.1996, there was no allegation or complaint of any illegality or irregularity in the aforesaid 63 election centres. After re-election in the aforesaid 6 election centres on 19.06.1996 Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan was declared elected by a margin of 559 votes than the election petitioner Md. Ataur Rahman Khan. On 20.06.1996 the election petitioner raised objection to the Re-turning Officer and prayed for re-election in 68 election centres. Eight days after the election on 12.06.1996, the election petitioner raised so may allegations against the election of appellant Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan. He stated that elections were held peacefully in all the election centres with the help of Police, B.D.R. and other agencies of the Government under the supervision of Magistrate. There was no rigging at all in the aforesaid election centres. In Shatgram election centre out of 3393 votes, 2651 votes were cast and Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan got 2167 votes and election petitioner got 438 votes. He further stated that in order to hold peaceful election Army was deployed and the observers also saw the holding of election who reported that everywhere election was held peacefully. Out of grudge, enmity and party rivalry the instant election petitioner had no supporter in Shambupura and Domar Char election centres the election petitioner got nil vote.

6. In the back ground of the aforesaid pleadings 8 issues were framed by the Election Tribunal. The election petitioner examined 6 witnesses including himself and the respondent No. 1 -appellant Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan examined 21 witnesses including himself. Both the parties adduced papers and documents which have been marked as exhibits.

7. After discussing the material evidence on record and hearing the parties and also recounting the ballot papers of Shambupura and Domar Char election centres the Tribunal held that in Shambupura election centre 260 votes and in Domar Char election centre 1151 votes were illegally counted in favour of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan and as such in total 1411 votes were liable to be cancelled from the account of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan and thereby Election Tribunal deducted 1411 votes of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan and declared Md. Ataur Rahman Khan as an elected Member of the Parliament from the aforesaid constituency by a margin of 852 votes. Being aggrieved by that Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan preferred First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 44 of 1999.

8. Before considering the question of recounting of votes cast in the aforesaid two centres in favour of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan, let us consider first as to what are the allegations made in the election petition and proved by the oral evidence of the relevant P.Ws. and what are the defence evidence in favour of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan.

9. In the election petition it was alleged that in Shambupura, Domar Char and Khaliar Char election centres there were total riggings, and the musclemen and supporters of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan forcibly entered into the election centres and drove out the agents of other candidates and in connivance with the election officers rigged the polls and illegally put seals on "Boat Symbol" on several hundreds of ballot papers and entered the same in the ballot boxes. P.W. 1 Md. Ataur Rahman Khan stated that in Shambupura School Centre Younus Mollah was his poling agent, in Domar Char Centre Touhidul Haque was his polling agent and in Khaliar Char Sona Miah was his polling agent. But this P.W. 1 the election petitioner did not disclsoe the aforesaid names in the election petition who allegedly stated that in the aforesaid election centres agents of other candidates were driven out from the election centres and they lodged complaint in writing to the concerned Presiding Officers about the vote rigging, but it was not accepted by the concerned Presiding Officers.

10. P.W.2 is Touhidul Huq who was the alleged polling agent of election petitioner in Domar Char election centre. He stated that on pistol point he was driven out from the election centre and the supporters of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan illegally put seals on "Boat Symbol" on several hundred ballot papers and put the same in the ballot box. He lodged written complaint to the Assistant Presiding Officer, but he refused to accept the same. After election he gave the petition of complaint to the election petitioner who submitted the same before the Election Tribunal which were marked as Exts. 2 and 2(1). In cross-examination he stated that he did not know the Presiding Officer of that centre. He hails from village Elamdi, P.S. Araihazar. In Domar Char election centres P.W. 14 Abdul Awal was the Presiding Officer and he hails from village Elamdi, P.S. Araihazar. Being the inhabitant of the same village this P.W. 2 stated that he did not know P.W. 14, the Presiding Officer, who is a Head Master of a school and he belonged to his own village. So, it appears that this P.W. 2 made a total false statement before the Tribunal.

11. P.W. 4 Yunus Mollah was the polling agent of election petitioner in Shambupura election centre. This P.W.4 also hails from village Elamdi. He stated that he was the polling agent in Shambupura election centre on behalf of Md. Ataur Rahman Khan. But the musclemen of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan drive him out from the election centre and they put seals on several hundred-ballot papers on "Boat Symbol" and put the same in the ballot box. He further stated that he made written complaint to the Assistant Presiding Officer about his rigging but the Assistant Presiding Officer refused to accept it. Thereafter he gave it to election petitioner who filed the same before the Election Tribunal and the same were marked as Exits. 5 and 5(1). Now it appears that P.W. 1 election petitioner, P.W. 2 polling agent in Domar Char centre and P.W. 4 polling agent in Shambupura election centre belonged to the same village Elamdi. He stated that Shambupura election centre is situated within the local area of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan.

12. Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan is R.W. 1. He denied all the aggregations made against his election in the aforesaid election centres. It is his case that in all the election centres election was held peacefully with the help of Police, B.D.R. and Magistrate who were on whole time duty and the army people were also patrolling the election centres. According to him, in the Shambupura and Domar Char election centres there were no rigging or malpractice or corrupt practice during the election under the supervision of a Magistrate.

13. In Shambupura election centres R.W. 15 was the Presiding Officer, R.W. 14 was the Presiding Officer of Domar Char election centre. These two important witnesses stated that there were no disturbances at all in Shambupura and Domar Char election centres and further told that the election was held peacefully and no complaint from any quarter was lodge to them. They fully corroborated with the evidence of R.W.1 Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan. Further R.W.3, R.W.4 and R.W. 5 corroborated with the evidence of R.W.1, R.W.14 and R.W. 15 that elections in the above two election centres were held peacefully and there was no disturbance at all. Further R.W.6, R.W.7 and R.W.10 also corroborated with the evidence of R.Ws. 1 and 14 about election in Domar Char centre. R.W. 10 formerly a Member of Parliament of B.N.P. deposed in favour of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan. He stated that there was peaceful election in Domar Char election centre.

14. From the judgment of the election case it apepars that the Tribunal has decided the case on recounting the ballot papers of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan only in Shambupura and Domar Char election centres. As regards rigging in the election of the aforesaid two centres we have already discussed above. Mr. Amir-ul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant, submits that in the election petition the allegations are absolutely vague and indefinite and no description of specific allegation has been incorporated therein. In this connection he has drawn our attention to Articles 51, 58 and 63 C.D. (2) of Representation of the People Order, 1972, (P.O. 155 of 1972). He submits that in order to establish an election case the allegation must be specific and it must be proved by specific evidence in support thereof but in the instant case no such allegations giving particulars of election offences have been given in the election petition itself.

As regards Shambupura election centre evidence were given by P.W. 1 and P.W.4,.P.W. I is the election petitioner Md. Ataur Rahman Khan and P.W.4 Md. Yunus Mollah was allegedly his milling agent in Shambupura election centre. The name of this polling agent Md. Yunus Mollah was not mentioned in the election petition. Further, this P.W. 1 Md. Ataur Rahman Khan, the election petitioner and this P.W.4 Yunus Mollah belonged to the same village Elamdi. They tried to prove rigging in election centre Shambupura. On the other hand, R.Ws. 1,3,4,5,8 and 15 deposed before the Tribunal that the election in Shambupura centre was held peacefully and there was no disturbance at all. Among the R.Ws. R.W. 15 was the Presiding Officer who categorically stated before the Tribunal that election was held peacefully in Shambupura election centre. In view of the depositions of the aforesaid R.Ws. it appears to us that P.Ws. 1 and 4 have totally failed to prove rigging in the election centre at Shambupura. As such, the findings of rigging in Shambupura election centre made by the Election Tribunal are totally contrary to the evidence of R. Ws, Among the R.Ws., R.W. Nos. 3, 4, 8 and 15 are quite independent and disinterested witnesses. In this view of the matter we hold that the election petitioner Md. Ataur Rahman Khan totally failed to prove that there was election rigging in Shambupura election centre.

16. About the allegations of rigging in Domar Char election centre P.W. 1, the election petitioner and P.W.2 Touhidul Haque came to depose that there was total riging in the election in Domar Char Centre. This P.W.2 Touhidul Haque was the polling agent of election petitioner at Domar Char. Both the election petitioner Md. Ataur Rahman Khan and Touhidul Haque, P.W.2 hail from the same village Elamdi. P.W. 2 and R.W.14, who was Presiding Officer at Domar Char election centre, also belonged to the same village Elamdi. But P.W.2 Touhidul Haque stated that he did not know the Presiding Officer of Domar Char. This shows that this P.W. 2 made absolutely false statement before the Tribunal by stating that he did not know R. W.14, the Presiding Officer of Domar Char centre though he belonged to the same village Elamdi. Further, R.Ws. 1, 6, 7, 10 and 14 categorically stated before the Tribubal that there was no disturbance and election was held peacefully in Domar Char centre with the help of law enforcing agencies, but on behalf of election petitioner only he himself as P.W. 1 and polling agent P.W. 2 alleged that there was rigging in election centre at Domar Char. Analysing the depositions of P.Ws. 1 and 2 and the depositions of R.Ws. 1, 6, 7, 10 and 14 it appears to us that the election petitioner had totally failed to prove disturbance and election rigging in Domar Char election centre.

17. Mr. Islam submits that election in the aforesaid two centres was held on 12.06.1996. Out of 69 election centres only there were disturbances in 6 centres and there were no disturbances in 63 other election centres including these two centres Shambupura and Domar Char. The election petitioner only alleged rigging and disturbance in these two election centres in his election petition only. But he did not raise any objection about alleged rigging in election in the aforesaid two centres either to the respective Presiding Officers or to the Returning Officer before filing the election petition. So, the allegations of rigging, disturbance and other corrupt practices in the aforesaid two election centres were an afterthought, which have no basis at all. We find force in the above submissions of Mr. Islam, and as such we hold that the election petitioner totally failed to establish rigging and other corrupt practices in the above two election centres.

18. Let us now come to the question of recounting of ballot papers of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan in the aforesaid two election centres. Mr. Amir-ul-Islam, the learned Advocate submits that in the aforesaid two election centres election was hold on 12.06.1996 and just at the time of election or just after the election, neither the election petitioner nor his election agents raised any objection about counting of ballot papers nor they applied to the Presiding Officers or Returning Officers for recounting of the ballot papers for the alleged irregularities. So, no case has been made out for recounting the ballot papers of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan.

19. He further submits that when re-counting was allowed in the aforesaid two centres ballot papers of all the contesting candidates ought to have been recounted. But unfortunately the ballot papers in which the seals were put on "Boat Symbol" only were recounted. But the ballot papers of other candidates were not touched and counted by the Tribunal. He further submits that there must be a satisfaction for the Tribunal that the election dispute cannot be decided unless re-counting is made. Only in such case recounting is necessary. So the Tribunal went beyond its jurisdiction to recount only the ballot papers carrying seals on "Boat Symbol" only and such action is absolutely illegal and without jurisdiction.

20. In this connection we may refer to Order No. 77 dated 9.12.1998 passed by the Election Tribunal where the prayers were made for recounting of ballot papers of Shambupura, Domar Char, Shatgram and Khaliar Char election centres. After discussing the materials and hearing the parties the Tribunal held that in order to arrive at a correct decision and for ends of justice the re-counting of ballot papers of Shambupura and Domar Char election centres was necessary in the facts and circumstances of the case. The appellant Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan did not challenge the order dated 09.12.1998 at that stage and as such, now he is debarred from challenging the recounting the votes of the aforesaid two election centres. Since Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan, the appellant had accepted the aforesaid order of the Election Tribunal without any protect, we find that such prayer cannot be reopened now before the appellate Court at this stage. Tribunal re-fused to recount the ballot papers of Shatgram and Khaliar Char election centres by the same order. Order No. 77 dated 9.12.1998 passed by the Tribunal runs as follows:

৭৭ (৯/১২/১৯৯৮) অদ্য মোকাদ্দমা সংক্রান্ত বিরোধীয় নির্বাচনী এলাকায় ভোটকেন্দ্র সমূহের নির্বাচনী উপকরণ তলব সংক্রান্ত আদেশের জন্য ধার্য আছে। উভয়পক্ষ হাজিরা দাখিল করিয়াছে। অত্র ��োকাদ্দমার বিগত ১৮/১১/১৯৯৮ ইং তারিখ যুক্তিতর্ক শুনানী সমাপ্ত হয়। গত ২৪/০৯/৯৭ ইং তারিখ প্রার্থীপক্ষ বিরোধীয় নির্বাচনী এলাকায় শম্ভুপুরা, ডোমার চর, খালিয়ার চর এবং সাতগ্রাম এর ব্যালট পেপার অন্যান্য কাগজাদি অত্র আদালতে তলবক্রমে উক্ত ভোটকেন্দ্র সমূহের ভোট পুন:গণনার জন্য আবেদন করেন ৷ অপর পক্ষের ৰিজ্ঞ কৌশলী উক্ত দরখাস্তের উপর আপত্তি উতথাপনক্রমে উল্লেখ করেন যে, উল্লেখিতকেন্দ্র সমূহে নির্বাচনী উপকরণ তলব করার আইনত: কোন যুক্তিসংগত কারণ নাই ৷

দরখাস্তকারী তাহার মূল দরখাস্তের প্রর্থনায় উপরোক্ত ৪ টি কেন্দ্রে নির্বাচনী উপকরণসমূহ আদালতে তলবক্রমে অত্র মোকাদ্দমা নিস্পত্তির জন্য প্রার্থনা করেন । অত্র মোকাদ্দমায় উভয় পক্ষ দাখিলকৃত কাগজ-পত্রাদি এবংসাক্ষ্য পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে,১ নং প্রতিপক্ষ শম্ভুপুরা এবং ডোমার চর কেন্দ্রে ১৭৪০ এবং ২১০০ ভোট প্রাপ্ত হন এবং প্রার্থীকে ০ (শুন্য) ভোট প্রাপ্ত দেখানো হইয়াছে। অপরদিকে প্রার্থীকে কালিয়ারচর ২৮৯ এবং ১নং প্রতিপক্ষকে ১৩৪৭, সাতগ্ৰাম কেন্দ্রে প্রার্থীকে কালিয়ারচর ৪৩৯ এবং ১নং প্রতিপক্ষকে ২১৩০ ভোট প্রাপ্ত দেখানো হইয়াছে।

উপরোক্ত অবস্থার পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে শম্ভুপুরা এবং ডোমোরচর কেন্দ্রে প্রার্থী পক্ষে (কান ভোট বাস্তবে প্রদত্ত হইয়াছিল কিনা বা তাহার নামীয় কোন ভোট ১নং প্রতিপক্ষের নামে গণনা করা হইয়াছে কিনা তাহা ন্যায় বিচারের স্বার্থে পূণঃ পরিক্ষা-নিরীক্ষা করা প্রয়েজেন বলিয়া আমার কাছে প্রতীয়মান হইতেছে যাহার অনুপস্থিতিতে অত্র মোকাদ্দমা চূড়ান্তভাবে নিষ্পত্তি অসম্ভব ৷ অপরদিকে সাতগ্রাম এবং কালিয়ারচর ভোটকেদ্রে গৃহীত ভোট সমূহ পুন:গণনা করা আবশ্যক বলিয়া আমার কাছে প্রতীয়মান' হয় না ।

অতএব, আদেশ হয় যে, জাতীয় সংসদ আসন-২০০৩, নারায়নগঞ্জ-২, আড়াই হাজার নির্বাচনী এলাকার অন্তর্ভূক্ত শম্ভুপুর উচ্চ বিদ্যালয় এবং ডোমোরচর সরকারী প্রাথমিক বিদ্যালয় ভোট কেন্দ্রসমূহের ব্যবহৃত অব্যহৃত, টেন্ডার, পোষ্টাল ব্যালট পেপারসহ ব্যালট পেপারের ব্যবহৃত কাউন্টার ফয়েলসহ প্রিজাইডিং অফিসার কর্তৃক দাখিলী ফলাফল বিবরনীসহ যাবতীয় নির্বাচনী উপকরণসহ আগামী ২১/১২/৯৮ইৎ তারিখের মধ্যে অত্র আদালতে প্রেরণ করার জন্য নারায়নগঞ্জের রিটার্নিং অফিসার এবং জেলা প্রশাসককে নির্দেশ দেওয়া গেল ৷ অন্যথায় আইনত: অকার্য হইবে৷ বিশেষ বাহকের খরচা বাবত টা:২০০/- (দুইশত) টাকা প্রার্থী দরখাস্তকারীকে জমা দেওয়ার জন্য আদেশ দেওয়া হইল ।আগামী ধার্য তারিখ পূনঃআদেশ ৷

স্বাক্ষর/অষ্পষ্ট

জজ, নির্বাচনী ট্রািইবুনাল, ঢাকা।

21. Let us now consider as to whether the Election Tribunal had legally recounted the Ballot papers of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan. From the running page Nos. 291 and 292 of the paper book, Part-1 it appears that the Tribunal examined the ballot papers having "Boat Symbol" of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan of booth Nos. 1,2,3 and 4 of Shambupura centre and found that 22 ballot papers were liable to be cancelled as the same did not bear signatures of Assistant Presiding Officer. Such cancellation of 22 ballot papers is illegal inasmuch as law does not require Assistant Presiding Officer's signature on the ballot papers. Articles 36(4)(c)(1) of Presidents' Order No. 155 of 1972 provides that a ballot paper shall be cancelled if it does not bear official mark. Only in the Guide Lines given by the Election Commission it is provided in para No. 5,7,1 (Ga) that a ballot paper will contain on its back official mark and signature of Assistant Presiding Officer. As it is a Guide Line given by the Election Commission and as it is not a part of the statute, such signature on the back of the ballot paper is directory, but not mandatory. A ballot paper having official mark only, not signed by the Assistant Presiding Officer, can not he declared invalid. So, we hold that cancellation of the aforesaid 22 ballot papers of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan at Shambupura election centre is illegal and void.

22. In the said Shambupura election centre in Booth No. 1,2 and 3, 1751 ballot papers thumb impressions were given and on the counterfoils of 27 ballot papers signatures were given (vide page Nos. 292-294 of Paper Book, Part-1). Further, it is found by the Tribunal that special forms No. I, 2 and 3 were not properly maintained by the Presiding officer with regard to the election of Shambupura election centre. But we find that these are more technical irregularities of the Officers, not at all concerned with the validity of ballot papers. Relying upon such irregularities together with the fact that out of 1751 counterfoils, 1724 counterfoils bore thumb impressions and 27 counterfoils bore signatures, the Tribunal abruptly held that 260 ballot papers having "Boat Symbol" were invalid without showing any reasons whatsoever. Further, the Tribunal had not specified any reason as to how these 260 ballot papers out of 1724 having thumb impressions could be identified and declared invalid. Such finding of the Tribunal is absolutely vague, indefinite, unspecified and not based on any material evidence on record and as such we hold that the cancellation of 260 ballot papers is absolutely illegal and void.

23. As regards recounting of ballot papers of Domar Char centre it appears that the Tribunal considered the counterfeit of ballot papers void running pages No. 301-303 of Paper Book, Part-1 as per serial Nos. 1-17. Some of the counterfoils contained only official mark and some contained official marks and signatures. But it appears that all the counterfoils contained official mark which is the requirement of law vide Article 31(2)(2) of Presidents' Order No. 155 of 1972. Putting signature of Presiding Officer on counterfoil of a ballot paper is not required by law or by the Guide Lines issued by the Election Commission. If any signature is given by the Pre-siding Officer on the counterfoil, it is absolutely redundant for which ballot paper can not be cancelled. A ballot paper shall be cancelled if it does not bear official mark. All the counterfoils bore the official marks.

24. Regarding further recounting of ballot papers of Domar Char election centre the Tribunal has shown cancellation of 1151 ballot papers vide Paper Book, Part-1, pages No. 304 to 306, as per serial Nos. 1-15. In this election centre the ballot papers of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan were cancelled bumbering 1151, but we ourselves scrutinised and considered the reason for cancellation of the ballot papers as made by the Election Tribunal and it appears to us that only 92 ballot papers vide serial Nos. 2, 3, 4, 11, 14 and 15 were liable to be cancelled and other ballot papers of serial Nos. 1.5,6,7,8, 9, 10, 12 and 13 could not be cancelled as the same had borne the official marks properly. In some of the ballot papers one official mark was given and some of the ballot papers had borne more than one official mark. These ballot papers though valid have been illegally cancelled by the Tribunal. So, we hold that out of 1151 cancelled ballot papers only 92 ballot papers can be legally cancelled and the remaining 1059 ballot papers, in our view, were illegally cancelled, and as such these 1059 ballot papers are declared valid and the same should be counted in favour of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan.

25. Mr. Khondoker Mahbubuddin Ahmed submits that the ballot papers having two official marks should be cancelled. He further submits that the Tribunal after seeing ballot papers had cancelled the same and the appellate Court should not interfere with it. It is difficult for us to accept the above contention of Mr. Khondoker Mahbubuddin Ahmed. In this connection we may refer to Article 36(4)(c)(1) of President's Order 155 of 1972 which provides that a ballot paper shall be cancelled which does not bear official mark. But all the above 1059 ballot papers carried official mark according to law. So, we hold that in counting the ballot papers of Shambupura election centre and Domar Char election centre only 92 ballot papers of Domar centre are liable to be cancelled. Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan won the election by a margin of 467 votes. So, it appears to us that in total Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan obtained 58,825 valid votes and the other contesting candidate Md. Ataur Rahman Khan got 58,388 and as a result Tribunal's declaration of election of Md Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan illegal and declaration of Md. Ataur Rahman Khan as elected Member of Parliament from the aforesaid constituency cannot be sustained in law and as such, the same are liable to be set aside.

26. Mr. Khondoker Mahbubuddin Ahmed submits that Md. Ataur Rahman Khan has filed a separate appeal namely, First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 67 of 1999 against the same judgment of the Election Tribunal. He prays that ballot papers of Shatgram and Khaliar Char election centres ought to have been recounted. If the ballot papers of the aforesaid two centres were recounted his client would have been declared elected by a big margin of more votes. The Tribunal had committed wrong in not recounting the ballot papers of the aforesaid two centres and as such, the result of election has been materially affected. In this connection we may refer to the order dated 9.12.1998 by which the Election Tribunal after hearing the parties clearly held that recounting of ballot papers of Shat-gram and Khaliar Char election centres was not necessary at all. Election petitioner Md. Ataur Rahman Khan had not challenged that order at the appropriate time and now he is debarred from claiming recounting of the ballot papers of those two centres by the appellate Court. If Md. Ataur Rahman Khan was really aggrieved he ought to have challenged the order dated 9.12.1998 at the relevant time. So, it is difficult for us to entertain such objection now from Mr. Khondoker Mahbubuddin Ahmed for recounting the ballot papers of Shatgram and Khaliar Char election centres. Further, we hold that Mr. Khondoker has failed to make out a case for recounting ballot papers of the above two centres by the appellate Court.

27. Mr. Khondoker Mahbubuddin Ahmed submits that there was election rigging in Khaliar Char election centre and in this respect election petitioner Md. Ataur Rahman Khan had led sufficient evidence before the Tribunal. It is difficult for us to accept the above contention in view of the fact that the Election Tribunal has considered all the material evidence on record and thereafter held that the allegations of rigging and corrupt practices could not be established by the election centre. We have also considered the materials on record and found that there is no reason to have a contrary view to the findings of the Election Tribunal with regard to Khaliar Char election centre. The election petitioner had totally failed to prove the case of rigging or corrupt practice in Khaliar Char election centre.

28. Mr. Khondoker further submits that in Shatgram election centre rigging and corrupt practice were Rampant and Election Tribunal ought to have recounted the ballot paper of Shatgram election centre. Mr. Khondoker cannot now claim for recounting of ballot papers of Shatgram election centre inasmuch as the matter had been decided by the Tribunal by its order dated 06.12.1997 and as such, at this stage such objection cannot be entertained.

29. As regards rigging and corrupt practice in Shatgram election centre P.W. 1, the election petitioner and P.W.6 the polling agent of P.W. 1 deposed to the effect that there was total rigging done by the persons of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan. As against that R.Ws. 1,9,12,13, 18 and 19 stated before the Tribunal that election in Shatgram election centre was held peacefully and there was no disturbance at all. Of the R.Ws. R.W.18 was the Magistrate and R.W.19 was the Presiding Officer who was a Professor of a College. Both of them have clearly stated before the Tribunal that election was held peacefully and there was no rigging or disturbance. They further stated that the law enforcing agencies were alert and no disturbance was caused at any time during election. So, it appears to us that the election petitioner failed to prove any disturbance or rigging or other corrupt practice in Shatgram election centre. In this election centre there was disturbance on 12.06.1996 and that is why election of that centre was postponed and re-election was held on 19.06.1996. So, we hold that Mr. Khondoker has totally failed to prove any disturbance or corrupt practice in Shatgram election centre on 19.06.1996.

30. Mr. Khondoker further submits that in two election centres of local area of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan he got the highest number of votes but his rival candidate Md. Ataur Rahman Khan got zero vote. In Shatgram election centre Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan got 2967 votes and Md. Ataur Rahman Khan got 438 votes. In the local area of each candidate he usually gets highest number of votes and that may not be a cause for setting aside an election on the ground of corrupt practice or rigging. In the local area of Md. Ataur Rahman Khan he also got highest number of votes and the rival candidate Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan got insignificant number of votes.

31. Mr. Khondoker further submits that in several hundred counterfoils only the thumb impressions were given by the voters. This shows that there was total rigging in the election at Shatgram. The educated person cannot put thumb impression on the counterfoil of the ballot paper. Mr. Amirul Islam submits that the law prescribes that on the counterfoil a voter may give either thumb impression or signature. Even if an educated voter gave his thumb impression on the counterfoil, it was done in accordance with law and for such reason ballot papers could not be cancelled or it could not be presumed that there was rigging in the election in view of the fact that a great number of voters put their thumb impressions instead of signatures on the counterfoils. Article 31(2)(f) of President's Order No. 155 of 1972 provides that the election shall put his signature or thumb impression on the counterfoil of the ballot paper. At the time of election votes are being taken in such hurry that in order to save time an educated voter may put his thumb impression on the counterfoil of the ballot paper instead of signature and for that reason election cannot be vitiated or materially affected. So, the submissions made by Mr. Khondoker have no substance at all. In view of the above we hold that the election result of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan as a Parliament Member of the aforesaid Constituency had not been materially affected in any manner whatsoever and as such, his election as Member of Parliament should be sustained.

32. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, material evidence on record and the submissions of the learned Advocates of both sides and the judgment of the Election Tribunal, we hold that the impugned judgment of the Election Tribunal declaring Md. Ataur Rahman Khan as elected Member of Parliament from Constituency No. 203, Narayangonj-2, is absolutely illegal and void and as such the impugned judgment of the Election Tribunal is liable to be set aside.

33. In the result, First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 44 of 1999 preferred by Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan is allowed without cost and the impugned judgment dated 24.01.1999 passed by the Election Tribunal in Election Case No. 13 of 1997 is hereby set aside. Election of Md. Emdadul Haque Bhuiyan as member of Parliament from Constituency No. 203, Narayanganj-2, is hereby maintained. First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 67 of 1999 preferred by Md. Ataur Rahman Khan against the judgment of the Election Tribunal is hereby dismissed without cost.
